    #134164. Latest Update: How Many Flight Attendants Do Airlines Typically Hire In A Year?

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1500 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Simpleflying ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: How Many Flight Attendants Do Airlines Typically Hire In A Year?

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1500 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that cabin crew or flight attendant recruitment has always been extremely competitive, with thousands of people applying for a relatively small number of jobs.
    • In a recent development, this guide will look into the facts and figures around airlines and recruitment numbers and what we can expect in the coming years.
    • Recent findings suggest that across the aviation industry in the US, airlines generate around 18,500 flight attendant job openings per year on average.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that cabin crew or flight attendant recruitment has always been extremely competitive, with thousands of people applying for a relatively small number of jobs. Only a very small percentage make it through the complicated hiring process, and it's well known that it is easier to get into Harvard than to get a flight attendant job. Only between one and four percent of all applicants get the job.

    In a recent development, this guide will look into the facts and figures around airlines and recruitment numbers and what we can expect in the coming years. Will there be a shortage of cabin crew, and will the recruitment process have to change? How many cabin crew do airlines typically hire in a year?

    Recent findings suggest that across the aviation industry in the US, airlines generate around 18,500 flight attendant job openings per year on average. Each airline's hiring varies depending on fleet size, route expansion, and annual attrition rates. Major carriers such as Delta Air Lines, American Airlines, United Airlines, and Emirates routinely recruit between 1,000 and 5,000 new cabin crew members each year. This can rise up to 8,000 during major post-downturn or surges in fleet delivery.

    In contrast, smaller regional and low-cost airlines generally hire anywhere from a few hundred to around 1,000 cabin crew annually. This covers base growth and typical turnover rates of around 4% to 8%. Major carriers often receive upwards of 100,000 applications for just a few thousand spots, so hiring occurs in competitive, periodic windows that match aircraft deliveries and seasonal travel demand.

    The US Bureau of Labor Statistics states that there were 133,700 flight attendant jobs in 2025, and the employment of flight attendants is projected to grow 9 percent from 2025 to 2035, much faster than the average occupation. Many of those openings are expected to result from the need to replace workers who transfer to different occupations or exit the labor force, for example, when retiring.

    According to recent reports, despite the growing need for flight attendants, acceptance rates are extremely low, with 90% of applications being filtered out at the very first stage. Only 1% to 4% of applicants make the grade, and even then, not everyone completes training. It is a highly competitive career with many hoops to jump through. Emirates reportedly receives over 15,000 cabin crew applicationsevery month, according to Vertas Management. Just one percent of the more than 100,000 applicants get the job, according to Delta's hiring records obtained by FOX News. Major carriers like Delta frequently receive over 100,000 applications for roughly 1,000 to 1,200 roles.

    According to recent reports, the multi-stage screening process can take months, including screening, interviews, assessment days, online assessments, security checks, and medical checks, and often takes between three and six months. Even after that, there is a six- to eight-week training course that is heavily focused on safety and emergency procedures and aircraft equipment. Exam pass marks are very high, and there are only two chances to pass. Each batch usually loses a quarter of trainees during training.

    Industry observers note that airlines are very picky about their crew members and expect high standards of safety and customer service. Personal presentation is extremely important too, as cabin crew are the face of the airline and represent the brand as a whole. Airlines can afford to be extremely selective about who they hire because they know there will always be plenty of candidates available. Some people don't understand the true nature of the job and may leave during training or probation because it's not what they thought it would be.

    In January 2024, Emirates unveiled it was recruiting 5,000 cabin crew for 2024 to coincide with the arrival of the new A350 fleet. In 2023, they hired 8,000 cabin crew in 353 cities worldwide, creating a large and diverse workforce of 21,500 cabin crew as of August 2023. They are now estimated to have over 27,000 cabin crew. Emirates has reportedly changed its reapplication process from three months to six months, so a candidate can now apply only twice a year instead of four times a year.

    Sources indicate that american Airlines now employs just over 30,000 flight attendants, making it one of the largest cabin crew workforces of any airline in the world. The figure puts American ahead of rivals Delta and United, which each employ around 28,000 to 30,000 flight attendants. Southwest Airlines has around 20,000 flight attendants.

    According to recent reports, in 2025, Lufthansa recruited more than 2,000 flight attendants, according to Aeronews. Ryanair has over 16,000 flight attendants and is still recruiting for cabin crew. Qantas aims to recruit 600 flight attendants within five years to support its growing international network, according to Aerviva. The airline has also opened up a new base in Singapore. British Airways right now has around 15,000 cabin crew, with 12,000 being based at Heathrow, covering both short-haul and long-haul routes.

    Industry observers note that according to Aerviva, forecasts predict the need for over 1 million new cabin crew members through 2045, yet acceptance rates at major airlines remain under 5%. The International Air Transport Association (IATA) reports that international passenger travel demand is up 7.1% year-on-year and that it will double in the next two decades.

    In a recent development, boeing has also forecasted a demand for 1.02 million cabin crew members through to 2045, with around 40,000 openings every year to support fleet growth and replace retired crew or those who move to a different occupation. The global commercial aircraft fleet is projected to grow 2.4% annually through 2035, with widebody deliveries surging, particularly for US and Middle Eastern airlines.

    Under EASA and FAA regulations, one flight attendant per 50 passenger seats is required legally for safety in commercial operations. Taking that into consideration, and with expected aircraft deliveries, India and South Asia alone will need around 51,000 fresh cabin crew by 2044 as their fleets treble.

    In a recent development, delta describes a seven-week onsite training program in Atlanta for successful candidates. The airline's hiring process includes an application, assessment, virtual job tryout, on-demand interview, event-day interview, and a conditional job offer before training. Delta also states that its application window opens and closes according to operational needs. Candidates who are not selected should follow the reapplication period shown in the current requisition. Most airlines ask candidates to wait at least three to six months before reapplying.

    United has a 6.5-week training program in Houston after the selection stages. United indicates trainees become employees after graduating from training. The airline outlines the required qualifications and directs applicants to the posted role for current details. Requirements may change, for example, if they need speakers of a particular language or crew at a particular base. Applicants should read flight attendant postings thoroughly and check all working conditions before applying.

    Most candidates do not do the research to find out what the job really is, and that is one reason so many people fail to get a position. They see the uniform and glamorous destinations but do not see the long hours, relatively low salary, and complicated lifestyle. They also do not always understand that the primary role of the job is to evacuate passengers in an emergency or deal with medical emergencies and fire onboard.

    It has been revealed that global cabin crew openings are estimated at roughly 50,000 per year, driven by fleet growth and crew turnover or retirement. Airline recruitment is very dynamic and can change rapidly depending on fleet expansion. Regarding flight attendant recruitment, surges in hiring are also due to changes in airlines’ operational trends, expanding markets and networks, and shifts in candidate trends.

    According to recent reports, global cabin crew recruitment is experiencing a sustained hiring boom, with CAE's Aviation Talent Forecast projecting a need for 678,000 new cabin crew members globally by 2034. Over 60% of global demand (roughly 415,000 roles) is driven by replacing retiring or departing staff rather than pure fleet expansion, the report states. Asia-Pacific leads global demand (38% of projected hires), followed by Europe (142,000), North America (129,000), and the Middle East (95,000).

    Sources indicate that airlines are recruiting well ahead of the peak travel season; for example, airlines hiring in late 2026 are actively filling January/February training courses to staff summer 2027 schedules. Some airlines are closing their recruitment drives early, sometimes within 24 or 48 hours, because they have received so many applicants.

    Shifts in airline recruitment include attracting cabin crew over 50 in the UK. EasyJet has seen an increase in over-50s hired, double that of 2022, and a fourfold increase in over-60s hired. Some airlines have started funding their training courses, or paying a salary during training instead of it being unpaid as was previously. As airlines mostly expand premium cabins, recruiters are also looking to prioritize hospitality experience and multilingual skills. Some of the rules around gender-specific uniforms and visible tattoos and piercings have also changed in recent years.

    #134163. As a Solo Traveler, I’ve Booked Tours Around the World—But This Fjord Excursion in New Zealand Took My Breath Away

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1346 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cntraveler ↗ Open Full Page

    As a Solo Traveler, I’ve Booked Tours Around the World—But This Fjord Excursion in New Zealand Took My Breath Away

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1346 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • After taking the 17-hour Air Newly introduced Zealand flight from New York City to Auckland this May, I was determined to make the most of my first visit to New Zealand.
    • Industry observers note that I booked several day trips, from an Arthur’s Pass train tour starting in Christchurch to a Walter Peak farm tour in Queenstown.
    • Sources indicate that I was eager to see what “business class” would look like on a day trip, and the moment the doors to the Sprinter van opened, I was impressed.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    After taking the 17-hour Air Newly introduced Zealand flight from New York City to Auckland this May, I was determined to make the most of my first visit to New Zealand. I hopped around the North Island, relishing Auckland’s food scene, checking into the innovative Hotel Britomart, and visiting Wellington’s Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa. But when it came to the South Island, I realized the points of interest are far more spread out, with the massive Southern Alps to navigate through. The island has wide-open roads, but as an American conditioned to driving on the “wrong” side, I didn’t trust myself behind the wheel. So I turned to my favorite solution as a FOMO-fueled traveler who never wants to miss a highlight: scouring the GetYourGuide day-tour offerings to string together my ideal itinerary, a practice I’ve now participated in on all six continents.

    Industry observers note that I booked several day trips, from an Arthur’s Pass train tour starting in Christchurch to a Walter Peak farm tour in Queenstown. And while Upcoming Zealand’s natural beauty and the genuine Kiwi kindness made every experience enjoyable, the highlight was my grand finale: the Milford Sound Business Class small-group tour starting in Queenstown from a local operator called RealNZ. The round-trip 12-hour excursion brings guests in a glass-roof Mercedes Sprinter for stops along the iconic Milford Sound Road, then aboard a Milford Sound cruise through the fjord known as Piopiotahi in the Indigenous Māori language, which some consider to be the eighth wonder of the world.

    Check Availability at Get Your Guide.

    The wide-open views from the Sprinter van.

    Sources indicate that I was eager to see what “business class” would look like on a day trip, and the moment the doors to the Sprinter van opened, I was impressed. Each of the 14 black leather seats had a gray lambswool blanket, a plush green pillow, and a bottled shot of Manuka ginger Vitamin C boost juice. As a ginger shot addict who’s constantly searching for the best natural pick-me-up around the world, it was love at first sight.

    The long journey ahead—five hours each way—immediately shrank as our amicable guide provided context about where we were, explaining Milford Sound’s history, ecosystems, and Indigenous Māori connections. When all was quiet in the car, there was Starlink Wi-Fi to keep travelers entertained by their screens. After a quick refresher stop an hour in at the rural settlement of Garston, we reached the lakeside town of Te Anau, where one of its downtown shops served as our business class lounge.

    In a recent development, here, the coffee order I’d requested at the top of the day was already waiting in a covered reusable mug with my name on it, alongside a plate of pastries. It wasn’t long before we entered Fiordland National Park, part of the UNESCO World Heritage site Te Wahipounam. I looked up through the translucent roof as foliage from both sides of the road enveloped our van, winding through the gentle curves.

    Emerging through the Homer Tunnel, the writer stopped for this first glance of Milford Sound.

    Soon, the narrow road opened up, and we made our first stop at Eglinton Valley, an expansive glacier-carved flat where expansive fields of golden tussock grass are broken only by striking triangular peaks. Not long after were the aptly named Mirror Lakes, where the Earl Mountains are reflected near-perfectly in the glassy, still water; and Falls Creek, a craggy cascade that unfolds into a teal pond. During our stop at Monkey Creek, we spotted a couple of kea, the world’s only alpine parrots known for their playful behavior. Next, we drove through the Homer Tunnel, traveling less than a mile through the solid rock of Darran Mountain. Fittingly, our guide changed the soundtrack to the Jurassic Park theme as we dramatically emerged into Milford Sound at last.

    Industry observers note that as we descended through the twisty road into the Cleddau Valley, there were gasp-worthy sights at every turn. One minute we were heading toward a daunting granite mountain wall and the next we were looking out to the waters of the sound in the distance. After a quick stop at a bridge to catch a glimpse of Fiordland's highest peak, Mount Tūtuko, in the distance, we arrived at Milford Sound Visitor Terminal to board the MV Sinbad.

    A bridge across the Tūtoko River, which led to a view of Mount Tūtoko.

    The Cleddau Valley, with Milford Sound in the distance.

    That's when the premium service was cranked up a notch. After I was welcomed with a glass of local Cloudy Bay wine, I was led to my own bean-shaped wooden table with two cushy swivel chairs on one side and a couch on the other, set against expansive windows that stretched overhead for views of the peaks and falls.

    A trio of dishes containing local ingredients, curated by chef Tom Hishon.

    Then came the five-course tasting menu. Already waiting was a seeded sourdough bun with whipped kelp butter, and it was followed by Fiordland wapiti (a local deer) bone broth soup. Next was a trio of artfully plated bite-sized dishes: paua (sea snail) with black garlic, a bite-sized fried ball made of titi (a local seabird), and roe from Mount Cook salmon. The penultimate dish was wapiti (elk) tartare with potato crisps plus smoked eel. It was all capped off with a “flat white”—an ice cream–topped dessert playing off the popular coffee drink.

    It has been revealed that between dishes, the captain of the MV Sinbad talked us through the highlights of Milford Sound, steering us up close to its plentiful cascades, including Sutherland Falls (1,904 feet tall), Lady Bowen Falls (531 feet), and Stirling Falls (508 feet). When he noted that Niagara Falls is only about 180 feet tall, I thought I misheard and went over to ask. But despite the massiveness of Milford Sound, the falls exuded a calmness that overshadowed their height.

    The area is home to bottlenose dolphins, Fiordland crested penguins, and humpback whales, and we caught a glimpse of a New Zealand fur seal lounging at Seal Rock. Throughout the two-hour cruise, the peaks—some craggy and pointy, others smooth and sloping—were a reassuring constant.

    Industry observers note that feeling rejuvenated thanks to both the power of Mother Nature’s beauty and the gourmet dining, we eventually returned to the van, where a generously sized bag of Marlborough Sea Salt Proper Crisps was waiting on my seat along with a Whittaker’s bar, New Zealand’s most famous chocolate. Of course, since it is business class, I also received a refreshing hand towel as I boarded.

    As we began the journey back to Queenstown, I gazed upward, soaking in the view from the car’s glass roof, with a contented smile. A rest stop later, I was so relaxed that I drifted off into a deep sleep. The next thing I knew, we were back in the city. We had spent 10 hours out of the 12-hour trip inside the van, but I hardly realized it thanks to all the luxurious touches at every turn. In this case, the journey was absolutely part of the destination.

    In a recent development, the Milford Sound Business Class tour debuted in October 2025 as a joint operation between RealNZ and Altitude Tours. I originally saw the offering on GetYourGuide, my preferred tour booking platform for its flexible cancellation policies, but you can also book directly through the RealNZ website. The excursion starts at $383 per person for the business class tour, but a coach version is also available.

    In a recent development, the tour I took transferred from Queenstown, but RealNZ also offers the trip from Te Anau, as well as a self-drive experience. There’s also the option to book travel back to Queensland via a 45-minute flight in a fixed-wing aircraft for an additional cost, though it’s weather-dependent. For those seeking deeper immersion, there’s also an overnight cruise through Milford Sound, with the choice of private cabins with en suite bathrooms or shared bunk-style compartments.

    #134162. Citi Shop offers an easier way to save when shopping online

    Citi Shop offers an easier way to save when shopping online

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1046 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thepointsguy

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Citi Shop takes some of the work out of saving money online.
    • It has broad reach, too, with more than 5,000 participating online merchants.
    • Its ease of use makes it a great resource, but other portals or special discounts may save you more.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Citi Shop takes some of the work out of saving money online. Once you've installed its browser extension, it acts as a shopping portal and coupon hunter all-in-one, rewarding you with statement credits.

    It has broad reach, too, with more than 5,000 participating online merchants. That's easier than a traditional online shopping portal, which requires you to remember to start at the portal and click through before filling your cart.

    Its ease of use makes it a great resource, but other portals or special discounts may save you more.

    Here's how Citi Shop works and what to consider to determine if it's the best savings path for you.

    Sources indicate that citi Shop is a free browser extension for primary cardholders with an eligible Citi credit card, including ThankYou points cards and cobranded cards. Citi retail and commercial cards are usually ineligible.

    Offers come as either a percentage back or a fixed amount back, and your earnings are applied as a statement credit on the Citi card you selected during enrollment.

    Citi Shop is separate from Citi Merchant Offers, which requires you to enroll in targeted offers with a specific Citi card and then use that card for the qualifying purchase.

    Both Citi Shop and traditional portals give you an extra reward for making purchases they track.

    According to recent reports, but Citi Shop brings potential rebates to you, rather than requiring you to initiate your savings search. The extension automatically displays a pop-up with an available offer when you visit a participating website. You'll have the option to activate the offer before checkout.

    All of Citi Shop's rebates are provided as statement credits, unlike the potential airline miles, hotel points or credit card rewards of traditional portals.

    Sources indicate that what I like about Citi Shop is that it also acts like a shopping assistant. Instead of opening six coupon sites only to discover that every code expired last Tuesday, it handles the scavenger hunt for you and tests available promo codes on your behalf.

    It has been revealed that like Capital One Shopping, Citi Shop uses a browser extension. However, Capital One Shopping doesn't require a Capital One card to enroll and its rewards can be redeemed for eligible gift cards instead of a statement credit.

    It has been revealed that generally speaking, Citi Shop clashes with other shopping portals. Both work by referring and tracking your purchase, so they can be mutually exclusive. You'll need to make your purchase through whichever offer is better.

    Related: Chase shopping portal guide: How to earn bonus Ultimate Rewards points.

    Unless Citi Shop finds a promo code, it won't lower your total at checkout. Its returns arrive later as statement credits and may require patiently waiting two to six months, sometimes longer.

    Recent findings suggest that even though you need an eligible Citi card to enroll, you don’t have to pay with it. Citi allows any payment method accepted by the merchant.

    I really appreciate the flexibility to choose the best card for each purchase. For electronics, I might pick a card with an extended warranty while I might stick to a travel rewards credit card for hotel bookings. You can even pay with a gift card if you wish.

    Regardless of how you pay, the statement credit will post to the Citi card you enrolled.

    According to recent reports, if you have an eligible Citi card but rarely remember to click through a shopping portal, Citi Shop is an easy win. Install it, activate offers when the pop-up appears and let the credits come to you. That convenience can also be a significant benefit if you have partners or other family members who aren't as motivated to strategize on rewards as you are.

    But with a little extra effort, you might be able to earn even more. When the Citi Shop pop-up appears with an offer, take a minute to compare before you click Activate.

    Checking a shopping portal aggregator such as Cashback Monitor indicates payouts from multiple cash-back, airline and credit card portals, making it easier to compare a Citi Shop statement credit with points or miles elsewhere.

    Suppose a $200 jacket is marked down to $160. Citi Shop finds a $10 coupon, bringing the checkout price to $150, and offers 8% back. Assuming the full amount qualifies, you'd receive a $12 Citi Shop credit. If you pay with a card that earns 2% back and has an activated merchant offer for $5 off a $100 purchase, you'd collect another $8. After all the credits and rewards post, your net cost would be $130.

    In a recent development, read the terms before getting too excited. Some brands, products, gift cards or coupon codes may be excluded and you might not be able to stack every layer every time. Still, you can often use multiple discounts simultaneously for a better deal.

    Citi Shop is not a program for instant gratification. Citi says statement credits post 61 to 180 days after a completed purchase, though some can take longer.

    It has been revealed that in many cases, offers may show as pending long before they officially pay out, to account for potential returns. Hotel rewards may remain pending until after the stay. Eventually, you'll see it on your statement as "CITI SHOP STATEMENT CREDIT.".

    According to recent reports, if a credit hasn't posted after the expected window, contact Citi using the number on the back of your enrolled card. You may want to keep good records along the way, like a screenshot of the offer and an e-receipt from the purchase.

    Citi Shop's biggest advantage is convenience. It does the heavy lifting by reminding you to activate offers so you don't miss out on earnings from your online orders, while testing coupon codes along the way. The offers themselves may or may not be the highest available, but they are certainly the easiest.

    To truly optimize your returns, you'll want to compare Citi Shop earnings with those from other shopping portals — and stack other forms of saving along the way. But when that sounds like too much, the ease of this extension can still be a great way to tack on some extra returns.

    #134159. Breaking: The Right Tote Bag Is the Ultimate Travel Companion—These Are Our Editors’ Favorites

    📅 06 Apr 2020 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2071 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cntraveler ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: The Right Tote Bag Is the Ultimate Travel Companion—These Are Our Editors’ Favorites

    📅 06 Apr 2020 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2071 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

    ⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • If you’re looking for a bag so versatile it can be your go-to personal item one day and your grocery shopping companion the next, the renowned tote bag is the only option.
    • Though the design of a tote bag is inherently simple, our favorite brands have curated precise variations to suit every kind of traveler.
    • It has been revealed that coach has been a favorite brand of mine ever since I got my first little black bag as a teenager.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If you’re looking for a bag so versatile it can be your go-to personal item one day and your grocery shopping companion the next, the renowned tote bag is the only option. From early morning flights to daily office commutes, or even a packed Saturday afternoon at the farmers market, our editors are always relying on their favorite tote. The best tote bags hold everything from our laptops, headphones, and water bottles to sleep masks and our most-used beauty products. Whether you reach for a structured leather version to pack your essential items in or an oversized, canvas carryall for a day at the park, the functions of the right tote are infinite.

    Though the design of a tote bag is inherently simple, our favorite brands have curated precise variations to suit every kind of traveler. My favorite tote has been my everyday work bag for years, but it has also accompanied me on countless flights, weekend getaways, and last-minute happy hours. A reliable tote bag really can do it all. Keep reading to discover 15 of our editors' favorite tote bags and why we can’t live without them.

    It has been revealed that coach has been a favorite brand of mine ever since I got my first little black bag as a teenager. Though I still cherish that tiny bag, my most used Coach item is my leather tote. For years, the Nina Tote bag has been my reliable sidekick. I’ve had it for so long that Coach no longer produces it. On the bright side, the Maggie Tote bag is almost identical to mine and is just as practical. I have put my bag through anything and everything over the years, and there is very little wear and tear. The leather is structured and durable, yet flexible enough to fit everything I need without toppling over. With plenty of interior pockets, my necessities all have a place, so I never have to go digging through the bottom of my bag to find the right lip gloss. Not only do I love traveling with this tote, but it’s also my everyday work bag and my go-to for almost every kind of activity.

    According to recent reports, I've never really had a work bag that I truly loved until I tried this one from Cuyana. What I appreciate about the System Tote are the additional organizational accessories that you can purchase to add a bit more structure to the interior. Aside from lugging it to and from the office each day, I use this tote as a personal item on the plane and brought it with me on a road trip to Acadia National Park, and have found it to be the ultimate travel companion. The built-in interior pocket is perfect for storing essentials you need to reach easily, like your passport, earbuds, or some petty cash, and since the bag can be snapped closed, you don't have to worry about anything flying out. —Jamie Spain, travel bookings editor.

    Recent findings suggest that this bag is all about the pockets. No tote has ever kept me quite as organized as this one from MZ Wallace, a brand known for its signature quilted bags. It offers six interior pockets, five exterior pockets, and a detachable pouch, offering me a dedicated space for all of my essentials plus a whole lot more. I’m always impressed at how much this thing fits; an umbrella, my 13-inch laptop, a full change of clothes, and my lunch. The Medium Metro tote features ultra-soft shoulder straps, making it a go-to for commutes to the office. My favorite thing about this bag is how lightweight it feels even when full—it never digs into my shoulders or hurts my arms. More features that make this roomy tote a smart choice for travelers: a luggage sleeve, protective feet, and a detachable and adjustable crossbody strap. —Meaghan Kenny, commerce editor.

    Monos’s Metro Tote has been with me longer than most Upcoming Yorkers are in relationships. I’ve had this faux-leather cutie for nearly five years now, and it’s traveled with me through new jobs, new apartments, and plenty of new adventures. I actually bring it to work with me every day—the laptop sleeve and spacious interior keep me organized on my way to and from the office. —Hannah Chubb, senior commerce editor.

    I've received so many compliments on this gorgeous structured bag from Cuyana—it's been a great work bag, with plenty of space for my laptop, planner, Kindle, chargers, and other day-to-day essentials. I wasn't sure how well it would function as a personal item as there's not a zipper to fully close the bag, but on a flight to Aruba, I made use of the leather ties to keep items contained, and found it well-sized to slip under the seat in front of me, even with my toiletry bag and a sweatshirt stuffed inside. I'm also a big fan of the snap-to-close key leash, and the interior slips pockets and zipper pocket. —Madison Flager, commerce director.

    The bag is perfect in the way a red apple sitting on a teacher’s desk is perfect. It’s classic, without ornament, the kind of thing that expresses its utility in its design. It’s both ubiquitous and aspirational, stirring up images of a dreamy East Coast: a white-sand, Nantucket beach; a shabby, wood-planked boathouse on the coast of Maine; a Gothic-inspired Ivy League campus. I've used it as a carry-on item, a beach tote, and as a weekender. Simply having it out on display in your home has the power to imbue your space with a charming, outdoorsy vibe. —Jessica Sulima, commerce writer.

    Baggu’s Nylon shoulder bag is more durable than its canvas tote bags but equally as stylish. It’s slightly slouchy, slightly structured, and comes in the signature Baggu colors and patterns. The adjustable quilted shoulder strap allows for a crossbody fit, a must-have for me when I’m commuting into the office or walking longer distances (nobody needs their laptop sliding off their shoulder onto the sidewalk). The zip closure and interior pockets are handy for organizing miscellaneous goodies and preventing spillage. Plus, the lightweight material can easily be flattened to fit into my suitcase. I find myself continuously reaching for this multipurpose tote on my way to the gym, office, farmers market, and airport. —Hannah Towey, associate editor.

    In a recent development, just when I think I’ve run out of room, I haven’t. The expandable bottom of this Calpak laptop tote adds an extra four inches, allowing me to add last-minute essentials or souvenirs mid-trip. Like all products in the brand’s Luka collection, it’s made of a lightweight, ultra-soft, puffy exterior that makes carrying its handle easy. The material is also easy to clean—simply wipe away dirt or spills without a worry. Inside, there’s a padded 15" laptop sleeve, multiple side pockets, and a zippered section to keep smaller items organized. Another feature I love: There’s a zippered pocket on the outside that keeps my phone or passport secure, while still being easy to access. It’s a great tote for commuters and thanks to its luggage trolley sleeve, an ideal carry-on bag for travelers. —M.K.

    Sources indicate that as a shopping writer who is constantly running between the office, press previews, catch ups with friends and, of course, the airport, I need a bag with space for all the day’s exploits and then some. July’s Juliette Soft Work Tote is my perfect do-it-all companion. It’s beautiful—I’ve received multiple compliments on this bag as I’ve been whizzing around with it, and the divided interior is really clever. There’s a 14" laptop sleeve to keep tech protected—all the more vital when you’re headed on a flight— and there’s also a dedicated water bottle holder too. It has a wide bottom so your lunchbox can go inside flat, plus a key leash to stop the rummage for your house keys. Brushed gold hardware and a buttery-soft faux leather exterior mean it looks effortlessly chic at after-work drinks, and when I'm off to the airport, the removable trolley sleeve slides over my suitcase handle so I can breeze through the terminal. It is my favorite desk-to-departure tote bag. —Charley Ward, commerce writer, Condé Nast Traveller UK.

    My Strathberry Kite is my most-used travel accessory. Not only do I use it for day-to-day tasks, it comes with me on almost every trip (the exception being adventure travel), and most recently carried me through trips to Lisbon and Istanbul, where I spent weekends catching up with friends and sightseeing. It's an ideal size for a laptop, should you wish to take it, but fits in plenty of other necessary items, too (like flip-flops or ballet flats after hours of strolling through cobbled streets). I love the walnut color and the soft, supple leather. I'm sure this will be a favorite of mine for years to come. —Abigail Malbon, global audience development manager.

    When I first saw Parker Thatch offers its Jack Tote bag in this unique zebra and burgundy color combo, I knew it had to be mine. I never travel without animal print, and there was something about this colorway that felt perfectly understated yet maximalist. I found it online about a year ago, and it sold like hot cakes—and has been (devastatingly) sold out since. I received it as a sweet gift from my partner a few months ago, who had pre-ordered it to arrive right when it was back in stock. I've been using it as my go-to work bag ever since. It has an incredible amount of space and strength to carry all of my everyday essentials and then some—from my laptop and a book to makeup and toiletries. Because of its exterior fabric as hair-on cowhide, she just needs to be shielded from the rain a bit more than your average bag. If the design is calling your name on this bad boy, it’s well worth the splurge. —Jessica Chapel, commerce writer.

    Industry observers note that I love anything Longchamp, and this gorgeous beach tote from the brand is my cherry on top of any vacation outfit. It’s large enough to hold a full day’s worth of goodies (sunscreen! sweatshirt! beach read!), but fits on the shoulder with ease. Plus, the toggle on the front keeps things contained in the most Longchamp-esque way. —H.C.

    Industry observers note that after passing the gauntlet of a last-minute trip to the British Virgin Islands, I always keep the Foldie Travel Bag on me, whether it’s riding in my backpack during my daily commute or stuffed into my suitcase on longer hauls. The front pocket easily held my thick reading list and two Moleskine classic notebooks; the full 40 liters of space in the main compartment (with the expansion unzipped) fit a week’s worth of clothes, chargers for four different devices, and another bag filled with toiletry bottles, plus room to spare for souvenirs. Another perk: the two inner pockets and wet pocket proved useful in sorting out the bag’s increasingly chaotic contents. The luggage sleeve was a relieving bonus that allowed me to transfer the hefty weight of my zealous packing to my suitcase. —Kat Chen, editorial assistant, destinations.

    I absolutely love this tote. Whether I’m wearing it to the office or while traveling, it fits everything I need. Plus, it comes with a separate removable pouch that I use even when I’m not wearing the bag. This slouchy bag is super durable and matches any outfit. —Pooja Nayyar, associate social media manager.

    Sentimentality may cloud my vision, for the tote in my possession belongs to my late grandmother. And when I tell you I was complimented frequently for it while in Italy, I mean I felt I needed to use the bag to beat back admirers waxing: “Wow, is Vera Bradley back?”; “Is it reversible?!”; “The textiles are so beautiful.” I often caught myself fantasizing about dumping it upside down to perform a “What’s in my bag” for nobody in particular—so capacious is the tote that I was needlessly carrying multiple novels within and rarely remembered to leave my toiletry kit on the hotel bathroom counter where it belonged. Handy pockets ringing the interior are just icing, and would have kept my passport safely inside had I ever been moved to act on the aforementioned dumping. —Charlie Hobbs, associate editor.

    #134158. Here’s Why The Boeing 777X Won’t Let Pilots Take Off With Its Wings Still Folded

    Here’s Why The Boeing 777X Won’t Let Pilots Take Off With Its Wings Still Folded

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1504 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that the Boeing 777X cannot take off with its wingtips folded due to critical safety and aerodynamic reasons.
    • While the 777X is physically capable of remaining airborne with its wingtips folded, it is strictly prohibited and operationally restricted from doing so by both design and regulation.
    • Industry observers note that the 777X uses a revolutionary wingtip folding system designed and manufactured by Liebherr-Aerospace at its center of excellence in Lindenberg, Germany.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that the Boeing 777X cannot take off with its wingtips folded due to critical safety and aerodynamic reasons. The extended wingtips are essential for the 777X's designed lift and fuel efficiency. Taking off with them folded would significantly increase drag and reduce lift, potentially compromising the aircraft's safety during the critical takeoff phase.

    While the 777X is physically capable of remaining airborne with its wingtips folded, it is strictly prohibited and operationally restricted from doing so by both design and regulation. The aircraft is equipped with escalating warning systems that alert pilots if the wingtips are not extended and locked before entering a runway. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) certification requires these systems to effectively prevent the aircraft from taking off in a folded configuration.

    Industry observers note that the 777X uses a revolutionary wingtip folding system designed and manufactured by Liebherr-Aerospace at its center of excellence in Lindenberg, Germany. This system is a first for commercial aviation and allows the aircraft to maintain high-efficiency aerodynamics in flight while fitting into standard airport gates designed for smaller aircraft.

    Sources indicate that the 3.5-meter (approx. 11 feet) wingtips are operated by a complex actuation system that transitions them between folded (vertical) and extended (horizontal) positions. The movement is driven by a hydraulic power drive unit (PDU) and geared rotary actuators. The full transition takes approximately 20 seconds.

    Recent findings suggest that once extended, the wingtips are secured by latch-pin and secondary-lock actuators. During flight, the mechanism is mechanically locked with a large bolt and electronically isolated. This ensures the wingtips cannot move even if there is a power failure.

    In a recent development, A wider wingspan moves the wingtip vortices further away from the fuselage. This reduces the downwash on the wing, allowing it to generate more lift with less drag. The larger surface area creates more lift, reducing the thrust required from the GE9X engines to stay airborne. This results in a roughly 10%-12% improvement in fuel efficiency compared to previous generations and competitors.

    According to recent reports, the 777X integrates advanced aerodynamics with digital flight controls to deliver a ride that is significantly more efficient and comfortable than its predecessors. The extra span enables the 777X to climb faster and cruise at higher, more efficient altitudes where air resistance is lower.

    Recent findings suggest that made from carbon-fiber reinforced plastic, these wings are thinner and lighter than traditional aluminum wings. This allows for the massive span without a prohibitive weight penalty. With GE9X engines, these aerodynamics result in lower fuel burn than competing aircraft like the Airbus A350, and a 20% lower fuel consumption rate than the legacy 747, which it is designed to replace.

    The 777X features Smooth Ride Technology, an advanced fly-by-wire system adapted from the 787 Dreamliner, designed to neutralize turbulence actively. Hundreds of sensors detect air disturbances in real-time. The flight computer then automatically actuates the control surfaces, specifically the flaperons, to damp vertical motion and pitch that passengers feel during turbulence.

    It has been revealed that the highly flexible composite wings act like giant shock absorbers, bending and flexing during flight to absorb gust loads rather than transmitting those forces directly to the cabin. Beyond the ride quality,the 777X offers a lower cabin altitude (6,000 feet) and higher humidity. These environmental improvements, combined with 40% less engine noise, help reduce jet lag and physical fatigue on long-haul flights.

    The folding mechanism is not designed to handle the massive aerodynamic loads encountered during takeoff and flight while in the "up" position. Attempting a flight with them folded could lead to mechanical failure or the tips breaking off.

    According to recent reports, boeing integrated multiple fail-safes into the flight systems to prevent such an occurrence. If the wingtips are not extended and locked, the aircraft's takeoff warning system (required by the FAA and EASA) will trigger a loud alarm when the pilot adds power.

    Boeing implemented an electronic checklist that confirms the position of the wingtips. If the flight crew attempts to initiate a takeoff procedure, the system will indicate “incomplete” until the wingtips are extended. If the pilots begin to take off roll without extending the wingtips, the avionics in the 777x will no longer trigger an aborted takeoff once the plane reaches 50 knots ground speed.

    It has been revealed that interestingly, Boeing had already explored folding wingtips for the original 777 in the mid-1990s, even patenting a design. However, that version was heavy and complex; the technology only became commercially viable with the advancements in materials and actuation seen in the 777X. Combining advances in newly introduced material science with the newly acquired archives of McDonnell Douglas made it a natural evolution to develop the next-generation Boeing widebody with folding wings.

    In its 1997 merger with McDonnell Douglas, Boeing inherited the F/A-18 Super Hornet program. The pivotal deal that integrated decades of naval aviation expertise into Boeing’s defense portfolio. By combining with the storied warplane manufacturer, Boeing inherited a rich legacy of naval fighter jet engineering and design. Looking past the hornet, the annals of the McDonnell portfolio include the most mass-produced supersonic naval fighter ever made, the F-4 Phantom II.

    In naval aviation, wing folding is often a manual pilot action verified by ground crews. For the 777X, Boeing automated the process to reduce pilot workload: the wingtips automatically fold when ground speed drops below 50 knots after landing. Unlike the Super Hornet, where a significant portion of the wing folds, the 777X only folds the outer 3.5 meters (11 feet) of its tip. This minimizes the weight penalty and places the hinge where structural loads are lower compared to a mid-wing fold.

    The 777X incorporates "spill-over" benefits from military R&D, specifically in the use of high-redundancy sensors and fail-safe locking pins that ensure the wing is structurally one piece before the engines can reach takeoff power. Boeing had to prove to the FAA that its new commercial mechanism could withstand aerodynamic loads equivalent to a fixed wing, leveraging testing methodologies honed over decades of military carrier operations.

    In 1995, Boeing patented a design for folding wingtips on the original 777, but the proposal was abandoned because airlines rejected the idea. The primary reasons for its abandonment were the added weight, reduced fuel capacity, and increased maintenance costs associated with the design.

    The main objective was to allow the widebody aircraft to fit into existing "Code E" airport gates, as initial designs anticipated a wingspan that might exceed standard limits. The original proposal featured a hinge positioned closer to the wing root, with the outer 21 feet (6.4 meters) of each wing designed to fold upward.

    Industry observers note that airlines found the engineering solution overly complex. The hinge's location negatively affected fuel capacity and added significant structural weight, making the trade-offs in performance and cost unacceptable at the time. The concept was not entirely discarded and was later refined and implemented in the current Boeing 777X program, which features a much larger, more fuel-efficient carbon-fiber composite wing.

    In a recent development, the folding mechanism on the 777X is placed further out on the wing, which minimizes the impact on fuel capacity and adds less weight than the 1995 design. The 777X's wingspan is significantly larger than the original 777 and would fall into the restrictive ICAO Code F category without the folding tips.

    It has been revealed that the 777X's 11-foot (3.36 meters) folding wingtips reduce the wingspan to within Code E limits when on the ground, allowing it to use most existing airport gates. This makes the aircraft more versatile and avoids costly airport infrastructure upgrades that competitors like the Airbus A380 require.

    The 777X program is famously delayed by nearly a decade. Originally slated to debut in 2020 for launch customer Lufthansa, the enormous twinjet is not expected to enter full-rate production until 2027. Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg stated this year that the company has “a mountain of work” ahead of it for certification. These delays are in no small part due to the 737 MAX disasters, with two fatal crashes in 2018 and 2019 that caused the death of 350 Souls.

    As the legendary American planemaker has course-corrected in the years following the tragic mishaps of the latest and greatest iteration of the 737, narrowbody mainline airliner, the 777X program has faced additional headwinds. The organization refocused on quality control and pushed ahead to ensure that all airframes remain as high-quality as they have always been, since the days when passengers would say, "if it's not Boeing, I'm not going.”.

    The Dubai Airshow 2025 reaffirmed customer confidence in the 777X, as the colossal twinjet offers the only viable replacement for the world's aging fleets of jumbo jets, such as the Airbus A380 and the legacy Boeing 747. Emirates, which is the world's leading widebody operator, upped its order for 65 more of the forthcoming 777X. The aircraft promises to usher in a latest era of commercial aviation, which we look forward to witnessing when the day comes.

    • Gabe Evans, who lost reelection earlier this month, unveiled Monday a 2028 run from the neighboring district of fellow defeated Republican Rep.
    • “Now more than ever, Colorado needs conservatives in Congress who will fight to keep our border secure, cut taxes for working families, keep boys from dominating girls' sports and locker rooms, protect our water, and make energy affordable,” Evans noted in a statement.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Rep. Gabe Evans, here arriving at the Capitol in July for a House Republican Conference meeting, lost his bid for a second term representing Colorado's 8th District. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call) (Bill Clark CQ Roll Call).

    Sources indicate that colorado Rep. Gabe Evans, who lost reelection earlier this month, unveiled Monday a 2028 run from the neighboring district of fellow defeated Republican Rep. Lauren Boebert.

    “Now more than ever, Colorado needs conservatives in Congress who will fight to keep our border secure, cut taxes for working families, keep boys from dominating girls' sports and locker rooms, protect our water, and make energy affordable,” Evans noted in a statement.

    His announcement comes less than two weeks after he lost his bid for a second term representing the battleground 8th District in the Denver area. While the race had been considered one of the most competitive in the country, Democratic former state Rep. Manny Rutinel secured victory by 15 points.

    According to recent reports, as part of House Democrats’ massive midterm gains, they flipped three seats in Colorado. Boebert narrowly lost her reelection bid in the 4th District to Democrat Eileen Laubacher, while Republican Rep. Jeff Crank lost in the 5th District.

    Evans’ statement cited his ties to the 4th District, which encompasses the eastern part of the state and extends into the Denver metro area.

    “From Loveland to Lamar, I’m ready to keep fighting in the 4th District, where I grew up, and where my family has lived since 1976,” he said.

    The district has a deep history of voting Republican. Boebert won by 11 points in 2024 while Donald Trump carried the district by 18 points.

    Sources indicate that evans is far from the first member of Congress to switch to a district seen as more favorable to his party. Boebert herself shifted from Colorado's more competitive 3rd District to run for the heavily conservative 4th in 2024.

    The 4th District will likely be a top target for Republicans in 2028, and Evans’ campaign sought to portray him as a clear front-runner in what could become a crowded GOP primary.

    “Gabe Evans will enter 2027 and the race for Colorado’s 4th Congressional District with $300,000 in campaign funds and name recognition that no first-time candidate in the district could match,” his campaign noted in the statement. “Combined with his record as an Army aviator, police officer, rancher, and member of Congress, that gives him a head start in money, name recognition, and credibility before the field takes shape.”.

    A former state legislator and Denver-area police officer, Evans also served 12 years in the Army. He was first elected to the House in 2024, unseating Democrat Yadira Caraveo, and presently sits on the Energy and Commerce and Homeland Security committees.

    Laubacher, a Navy veteran who will take office on Jan. 3, is the first Democrat elected to represent the 4th District since Betsy Markey won her lone term in 2008. In response to Evans’ announcement, Laubacher’s campaign said she would be “focused on making Washington deliver” for district residents.

    “There’s real work to do: ending the war in Iran that Gabe Evans voted six times to continue, lowering the cost of groceries and fertilizer that his eight votes for the tariffs helped drive up, and protecting the rural hospitals across the 4th district he voted to gut,” Laubacher spokesperson Taylor Gillespie said in a statement.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Washingtonians have a upcoming option to Portugal next summer.
    • TAP Air Portugal will launch a new thrice-weekly service from Dulles International Airport (IAD) to Porto Airport (OPO) on March 30, 2027.
    • TAP, a Star Alliance partner of United Airlines, will fly an Airbus A321LR on the latest IAD-OPO route.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Washingtonians have a upcoming option to Portugal next summer.

    TAP Air Portugal will launch a new thrice-weekly service from Dulles International Airport (IAD) to Porto Airport (OPO) on March 30, 2027. Westbound flights will operate on Wednesdays, Fridays and Saturdays through the summer, and on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays beginning in October.

    TAP, a Star Alliance partner of United Airlines, will fly an Airbus A321LR on the latest IAD-OPO route. The long-range, single-aisle aircraft is fitted with 16 lie-flat business-class seats and 155 economy seats.

    It has been revealed that the upcoming Portugal route is the latest international addition at IAD. United intends to launch new service to Toulouse, France, in April and to Milan in May, using its new long-range A321XLR on the former route.

    International seats from IAD will increase nearly 7% in the first six months of 2027 compared to this year, schedule data from aviation analytics firm Cirium demonstrates.

    It has been revealed that IAD is undergoing a massive, $22 billion redevelopment to bring its infrastructure up to modern standards. The first piece — a 14-gate section of the new Concourse E that includes a new, large United Club — opened earlier in November. Future phases include a new international arrivals facility that would support additional long-haul growth.

    This content is hosted by Instagram.

    And if the redevelopment blueprint stays on schedule, IAD could retire its jet-age mobile lounges by the mid-2030s.

    TAP’s new OPO route complements its existing service to IAD from Lisbon Airport (LIS).

    Sources indicate that the state-owned Portuguese airline is in the process of being privatized as part of the Lufthansa Group. The German airline conglomerate plans to buy an initial 44.9% stake in TAP, aiming to close the deal by the first quarter of 2028.

    Lufthansa Group chief commercial officer Dieter Vranckx mentioned in October that once the TAP deal is done, Lufthansa intends to integrate the Portuguese airline into its transatlantic joint venture with Air Canada and United.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    American Airlines is making another change to its senior leadership team, with Chief Operating Officer David Seymour set to retire at the end of the year.

    Seymour will step down on Dec. 31 and remain with the Fort Worth, Texas-based carrier in an advisory capacity through the first quarter of 2027, CEO Robert Isom revealed Friday.

    It has been revealed that seymour has served as American’s chief operating officer since 2020. He joined the airline in 1999 and held various leadership positions overseeing technical operations, crew scheduling, and flight operations.

    “He’s the guy you want in the room when the stakes are high,” Isom wrote in a letter to employees.

    JonCarlo “JC” Gulbranson, American’s current senior vice president of operations, will succeed Seymour on Jan. 1. He will report directly to Isom and assume oversight of the carrier’s technical operations, safety, and regulatory compliance teams.

    According to recent reports, gulbranson began his airline career at Northwest Airlines in 2000 before joining US Airways in 2008. He helped oversee the integration of flight operations systems following the merger with American.

    Industry observers note that american will also move its corporate security team under its government affairs division. A new reporting structure for the airline’s regional operations will be revealed in December.

    “For nearly three decades, jet fuel hasn’t just been in my veins. It’s been part of my DNA. To this day, I wake up excited to get to work — which is just about all you can ask for in a job,” Seymour wrote in a LinkedIn post.

    The changes follow a broader management reshuffle announced in August as the carrier works to narrow its profitability gap with competitors Delta and United.

    11 Warm-Weather Destinations to Flock to This Winter

    📅 26 Sep 2025 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2666 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

    ⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that arguably the best way to overcome winter is to pretend like it’s not happening—i.e., jetting off to a warm-weather destination, where seasons are not taken very seriously and an outdoor adventure is always on the table.
    • Recent findings suggest that whether you’re interested in hiking to the wild and wondrous waterfalls of Puerto Rico’s El Yunque National Rainforest, snorkeling through the kaleidoscopic waters of Belize’s barrier reef, or simply want to kick back and relax with a dip in Costa Rica’s hot springs, these sunny locations are bound to cure those cold-weather blues.
    • When to go: JanuaryAverage winter temperature: 80–85 degrees.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that arguably the best way to overcome winter is to pretend like it’s not happening—i.e., jetting off to a warm-weather destination, where seasons are not taken very seriously and an outdoor adventure is always on the table. The best winter vacation destinations offer comfortable temperatures, off-peak advantages, and festive happenings. On this list, you’ll find some of the usual suspects, from Punta Cana to the US Virgin Islands, as well as locales you might not have considered (far too often, travelers forget vibrant Marrakech is a shorter-haul Mediterranean option).

    Recent findings suggest that whether you’re interested in hiking to the wild and wondrous waterfalls of Puerto Rico’s El Yunque National Rainforest, snorkeling through the kaleidoscopic waters of Belize’s barrier reef, or simply want to kick back and relax with a dip in Costa Rica’s hot springs, these sunny locations are bound to cure those cold-weather blues. So, trade your snow boots for flip-flops and get to plotting your next escape.

    When to go: JanuaryAverage winter temperature: 80–85 degrees.

    If you’ve been looking for an excuse to finally book that trip to Hawaii, shoot for after the holiday rush, when flights get significantly cheaper. January might be the start of rainy season in Maui, but the showers are often short and localized; for the most part, you’ll enjoy sunshiny days with temperatures that hover in the low-80s. Humpback whales make their way from Alaska around this time, and you can spot the giant beauties from Papawai Point on Honoapiilani Highway, an overlook facing the ʻAuʻau Channel. If you’re not afraid of big waves, heavy north swells at this time of year make for excellent surfing, especially at Ho‘okipa Beach Park. The Road to Hana, a scenic and beautiful drive at any time of year, becomes especially lush in the winter after the rain has fallen, and you’ll likely avoid the crowds too. Along the way, hit up sites like the Twin Falls or the black sand beach at Waianapanapa State Park.

    According to recent reports, where to stay: A Condé Nast Traveler Triple Crown winner, Hāna-Maui Resort, a luxurious off-grid escape, is the pot of gold at the end of the Road to Hana, while Hotel Wailea offers an adults-only vibe on the southwestern coast. Though much humbler, Jimi Hendrix’s former gingerbread-style home, now available for rent on Airbnb, is also a fair contender for your home away from home, surrounded by all kinds of fruit trees and perfectly positioned for daily rainbows.

    When to go: December–JanuaryAverage winter temperature: 65 degrees.

    According to recent reports, while you won’t be breaking a sweat in San Diego come December, it’s an excellent place to escape to around the holidays for festive fun in mild, mid-60-degree temperatures. The Parade of Lights is a classic seasonal event, when over 100 private boats get decked out in twinkling lights and sail around San Diego Bay (watch from spots like Shelter Island or Seaport Village on select nights in December). Between November and January, you can also enjoy ice skating without the chill at the Hotel del Coronado, where you’ll glide alongside the Pacific. They say San Diego sunsets are best in the winter, when the sun cuts a path closer to the horizon and there’s not as much coastal marine fog—one of the best places to catch one is Sunset Cliffs Natural Park on the Point Loma peninsula.

    Where to stay: La Valencia, otherwise known as the “Pink Lady” of La Jolla, is one of San Diego’s most iconic stays, and you might hear a seal or two barking in the distance. For unparalleled mountain views, consider this glass house overlooking Sweetwater Regional Park.

    When to go: December–MarchAverage winter temperature: 70–85 degrees.

    Recent findings suggest that for a Caribbean escape with outdoor adventure, cultural festivals, and farm-to-table splendor, head to Puerto Rico. From December to March, you can take advantage of the dry season on the island, which means your days won’t be interrupted by sudden showers. Holiday festivities continue well beyond Christmas, from Three Kings Day on January 6—the oldest of these celebrations takes place in Juana Díaz, with a reenactment of the Magi on horseback—to the San Sebastian Street Festival, when the namesake street in Old San Juan is filled with art vendors, live music, and plenty of mofongo (January 21–24 this year). Winter is also a great time to explore El Yunque National Forest when it’s not shrouded in unbearable humidity—hike to La Coca Waterfall, take in the green canopy from Yokahú Tower, and keep an ear out for singing coquí frogs.

    Where to stay: For luxe accommodations just a 25-minute drive from El Yunque, look no further than Four Seasons Resort and Residences Puerto Rico, which coordinates guided treks with a strong emphasis on Indigenous history. Condado Ocean Club offers direct access to the beach, while this lakefront retreat near Cueva Ventana and Arecibo Observatory is ideal for couples seeking verdant views.

    When to go: December–MarchAverage winter temperature: 85 degrees.

    Recent findings suggest that another destination where US travelers can leave their passports at home, the US Virgin Islands are a quintessential Caribbean paradise. December through March is peak season, and there are plenty of reasons why—no rain, calm seas, and temperatures that hover between 77 and 85 degrees, to name a few. St. Croix, the largest of the USVI’s three main islands, is defined by the white sands of Rainbow Beach, as well as its Danish ancestry, which you can explore at colonial-era sites like Fort Frederik and Fort Christiansvaern. St. John is filled with all kinds of natural wonders; take the Underwater Snorkel Trail at Trunk Bay to peer at parrotfish, or set off on the three-mile Reef Bay Trail to hike among pre-Columbian petroglyphs painted by Taíno Indians. St. Thomas is a bustling port with cosmopolitan charm, and you’d be well advised to sample a few conch fritters at Gladys' Café. Whichever island you choose, clear skies and turquoise waters await.

    Sources indicate that where to stay: One of Traveler’s favorite private island resorts (and the only one in the US Virgin Islands), Lovango Resort and Beach Club is located across St. John’s Caneel Bay and offers all kinds of eco-chic accommodations, from wooden treehouses to explorer-style tents. The Westin St. Thomas is set right in front of the harbor, with a stellar spa worth traveling for. For something a bit more intimate, this light-filled, two-bedroom cottage is just a five-minute walk away from Cruz Beach.

    When to go: December–FebruaryAverage winter temperature: 65 degrees.

    While temperatures do drop in Marrakech during the winter—the peaks of the Atlas Mountains will be blanketed in snow—you’ll see far more sun than in certain parts of the US; plus, it’s all the more reason to enjoy a steamy hammam. Winter is a great time to explore the city's popular sites with thinner crowds: comb through the medina’s bustling souks for fragrant spices and a pair of babouche slippers, take in the cobalt blue buildings at the Jardin Majorelle, or learn about one of France’s most legendary fashion designers at the Yves Saint Laurent Museum. Keep an eye out for the dates of the Marrakech International Film Festival, which takes place between the months of November and December—this year it falls from November 20 to 28, and features 76 films from 39 countries.

    Where to stay: Traveler contributor Jordan Lippe-McGraw is a big fan of this family-friendly villa, with a heated pool, hammam, and cinema room. A Triple Crown winner, La Mamounia is the city’s grand dame. As global features director Erin Florio puts it, “Every inch of this palatial property has been hyper-considered to make the guest feel as though they have arrived in some regal estate of an Arabian kingdom.” At the Royal Mansour, all riads come with 24/7 access to a private butler.

    When to go: December–AprilAverage winter temperature: 80–90 degrees.

    It has been revealed that the Arenal Volcano looms over Costa Rica’s La Fortuna region, heating its natural springs, and there’s a greater chance you’ll see it without cloud cover in the winter. For travelers seeking a combo of adventure and relaxation, La Fortuna (about a three-hour drive from San José) is well-suited for both. Hike through cooled lava fields at Arenal Volcano National Park or swim around La Fortuna Waterfall, then take advantage of nature’s healing powers at Tabacón Thermal Resort and Spa. For a truly memorable experience, book a tour with Arenal Horse Tours and ride your steed straight into the Arenal River for a refreshing dip.

    Industry observers note that where to stay: While Tabacón is perhaps the most iconic resort in the area, The Springs Resort & Spa is another great option, boasting two dozen hot springs, pools, and waterfalls spread across the 65-acre property. If you’re looking for something more intimate, this forest cabin features a private spring-fed pool, rain shower, and marked hiking trails—a one-of-a-kind off-grid retreat.

    When to go: December–AprilAverage winter temperature: 80–85 degrees.

    Though small, this Central American country offers a diversity of experiences, whether you want to take it slow in a charming fishing village or ascend newly introduced heights in the jungle. Perhaps the most popular destination on Belize’s tourism map, Ambergris Caye is a departure point for the country’s barrier reef—though just south of Ambergris Caye, Caye Caulker provides a nice alternative. While on the car-free island, book a tour with Ragga Sail Adventures for a half-day snorkel through Hol Chan Marine Reserve, the oldest marine reserve in the country. Further south in Punta Gorda, you’ll find rugged adventures and a strong sense of Mayan culture. Here, you’ll have access to several offshore cayes (Belize has hundreds of these small islands, brimming with marine life), from Snake Cayes to Sapodilla Cayes Marine Reserve; if you prefer jungle, take a boat tour through the Monkey River, or hike to the waterfall at Rio Blanco National Park. And be sure to explore the surrounding Toledo District for Mayan ruins, like the Lubaantun, which dates back to 700–900 AD and is also an excellent site for birdwatching.

    Where to stay: Nestled within the Belizean rainforest, Copal Tree Lodge’s jungle suites will make you feel as though you’re suspended among the trees. Wake up to the sounds of monkeys every morning, then take a farm tour around the surrounding property, where you’ll discover how cacao, vanilla, and sugar cane grow. Over in San Pedro, Alaia Belize is your luxury option, just 600 yards away from the barrier reef, while this tiny home will make you feel as though you’re vacationing in a fairy tale.

    When to go: December–AprilAverage winter temperature: 80 degrees.

    Sources indicate that december through April is peak vacation time in Punta Cana, when the rainy season has subsided and there’s not a cloud in the sky. With average highs in the 80s and average lows in the 70s, you’re likely to experience perfect weather during your stay. Come February, you’ve got a good chance of spotting some humpback whales if you cast your eyes off the coast of the Península de Samaná, where they typically pass through until April. The country also celebrates Independence Day in February—on the 27th, to be exact. Visit around that time, and you’re bound to run into a Carnaval parade or bachata dance circle. With the Cordillera Oriental mountain range looming in the background and a selection of cenotes around town—from Hoyo Azul to Hoyo Claro—mountain buggy excursions and diving adventures await even in the winter.

    According to recent reports, where to stay: The W Punta Cana redefines the all-inclusive resort as we know it with top-tier dining and some of the largest rooms in the country. Hyatt Vivid Punta Cana, which just opened its doors in August 2026, is another upscale all-inclusive in the area, boasting swim-out suites and a chic speakeasy. If you’ve got kids in tow but still want to experience the height of luxury, Eden Roc Cap Cana is a consistent Readers' Choice Awards winner. For a villa the whole family will enjoy, this eight-bedroom Airbnb in Tortuga Bay comes with a private pool.

    When to go: December–AprilAverage winter temperature: 70 degrees.

    Sources indicate that another prime location for whale watching, Baja California’s southern tip sees the migration of humpback and gray whales between the months of December and April (you might even elect to swim with whale sharks, too, which roam around the nearby Bay of La Paz around this time). You’ll have just missed the rainy season in November, making way for sunny, 70-degree beach days and not-too-chilly evenings. The creative town of Todos Santos boasts a number of art galleries to pop into, like Galeria de Todos Santos and La Sonrisa de la Muerte, while the Sierra de la Laguna mountains are home to stunning trails and swimming holes. If you’re a surfer, Playa Los Cerritos and Playa San Pedro offer some of Mexico’s best waves.

    Sources indicate that where to stay: Todos Santos is home to a number of cutting-edge boutique hotels. Hotel San Cristobal, with its vibrant interiors and delectably fresh seafood, perfectly embodies the bohemian vibes of this tiny surf town. Paradero Todos Santos, located on a five-and-a-half-acre farm, is designed around outdoor adventure: Pick the “Unbound” option, and surfing, hiking, and biking experiences will all be included in the nightly fare. If you prefer to go the rental route, this little bungalow is set among farmland in Pescadero, with its own private rooftop.

    When to go: December–FebruaryAverage winter temperature: 75 degrees.

    Miami is a good idea any time of year, but December through February is considered the dry season, promising temperatures in the mid-70s. Two key events pop up this time of year: Art Basel Miami, in December (4–6, this year), and the South Beach Wine & Food Festival, in February (running the 25–28 in 2027). But there’s always something to do in the Magic City, whether that’s taking a peek into the Pérez Art Museum, spending money in the Design District, or having a stroll through the Fairchild Tropical Botanic Garden.

    In a recent development, where to stay: To embrace the happy-go-lucky spirit of the locals, check in to the Goodtime Hotel and sip on a Purple Reign cocktail (co-owner Pharrell’s favorite drink) at the rooftop pool club. If you’d like to tap into the city’s Art Deco architectural history, stay at The Moore, where you’ll be close to Wynwood and Downtown Miami. This dreamy loft in Collins Park, just a short walk to the beach, is a good bet too.

    When to go: December–FebruaryAverage winter temperature: 85 degrees.

    Recent findings suggest that depending on where you’re coming from, Cape Town might be a little out of the way. But the US's winter is their summer, and with that comes sunny days and a dry, Mediterranean-like climate. Around mid-January, tourists start to flee and kids return to school, making popular attractions more accessible. Take a cable car (or hike, if you’re feeling bold) up to the famous Table Mountain, or drive to Boulders Beach, which boasts one of the last colonies of African penguins in the world. There are plenty of opportunities to engage with some art, as well, from the contemporary galleries at Zeitz MOCAA to the rainbow houses of the Bo-Kaap Museum. And if you’re feeling especially adventurous, you can treat Cape Town as a jumping-off point for the famed Garden Route road trip.

    It has been revealed that where to stay: For views of both Table Mountain and the V&A Waterfront, stay at the Silo Hotel, housed in a former grain silo and famous for its maximalist interior design. For something a little more off-the-beaten-path, Ellerman House is an Edwardian mansion turned boutique hotel situated in the exclusive Bantry Bay area. And if it's privacy you're after, this three-bedroom bungalow in St. James features a private hot tub and covered deck with gorgeous sea views.

    This article has been updated with upcoming information since its original publish date.
