    Some records in Ilhan Omar case will be released, judge states

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (470 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., speaks during a news conference at the Capitol last summer.
    • A judge stated he will order the release of some information about the federal investigation into Rep.
    • District Court for the District of Columbia made the statement Tuesday during a hearing brought by news organizations and an advocacy group seeking details about the search.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., speaks during a news conference at the Capitol last summer. Few details have emerged so far about the government’s search of her home earlier this fall. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    A judge stated he will order the release of some information about the federal investigation into Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., which included a search of her Washington house last month.

    Judge James Boasberg for the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia made the statement Tuesday during a hearing brought by news organizations and an advocacy group seeking details about the search. Boasberg ordered the government to provide him by Friday what could be disclosed in the case. He pointed to how investigators are handling the “speech or debate” clause immunity that Omar has as a sitting member of Congress.

    “This is purely legal questions, interesting questions, about the privilege, the extent of the privilege and how it would apply,” Boasberg remarked.

    The Constitution includes an immunity for members of Congress for the “speech or debate” they engage in as part of their jobs.

    Industry observers note that boasberg also directed the government to propose redactions to the as-yet secret docket. While he stated next week’s expected disclosures would not include the 67-page document that investigators provided to justify the search, he left the door open to unsealing that down the road if the government closes the case or brings charges.

    Justice Department attorney Alessandra Serano argued against broad disclosures, calling it “very rare that a precharging, pre-indictment unsealing would happen.”.

    The high-profile nature of the investigation leaked into the courtroom Tuesday, as Boasberg cited statements by President Donald Trump and others about the investigation into Omar.

    “You have had administration officials, prominent ones, talking about the purpose of the investigation,” Boasberg said.

    Administration officials have accused Omar of committing immigration crimes for years, and Trump noted last month the DOJ was looking into Omar “strongly.” Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said on a recent podcast that investigators had served multiple search warrants and were investigating possible immigration fraud tied to when Omar entered the United States as a child.

    Separately, Boasberg remarked he may matter rulings in the coming weeks unsealing portions of other court cases tied to the investigation, including one brought by Omar herself earlier this month seeking the return of the items seized in the search.

    Sources indicate that the administration executed the search warrant in October, just a few weeks before the midterm elections. The timing of the search drew accusations of political bias from Democrats who claimed that the administration brought the case to sway the midterm elections.

    For years Trump has said he wanted criminal charges to be brought against his political foes, including Omar and others in Congress.

    #134118. Amex Blue Cash Everyday Review: A No Annual Fee Card With Solid Bonus Categories

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2401 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Onemileatatime ↗ Open Full Page

    Amex Blue Cash Everyday Review: A No Annual Fee Card With Solid Bonus Categories

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2401 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • American Express is best known for its points-earning cards, but the Blue Cash Everyday® Card from American Express proves that Amex can do cash back well too.
    • It has been revealed that if you’re looking for a simple card that earns a solid return at supermarkets, gas stations, and online retailers, this one is worth a look.
    • This post is my in-depth Blue Cash Everyday Card review, so I’ll cover the bonus categories, the credits and perks, and how this card compares to both the Blue Cash Preferred® Card from American Express and the Citi Double Cash® Card.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    American Express is best known for its points-earning cards, but the Blue Cash Everyday® Card from American Express proves that Amex can do cash back well too.

    It has been revealed that if you’re looking for a simple card that earns a solid return at supermarkets, gas stations, and online retailers, this one is worth a look. It has no annual fee (Rates & Fees), a decent welcome bonus, a great intro APR offer, and some useful bonus categories that cover a good chunk of everyday spending.

    This post is my in-depth Blue Cash Everyday Card review, so I’ll cover the bonus categories, the credits and perks, and how this card compares to both the Blue Cash Preferred® Card from American Express and the Citi Double Cash® Card.

    Review: Learn more about the Blue Cash Everyday® Card from American Express.

    First, here’s an overview of the Amex Blue Cash Everyday benefits and value proposition, from fees, to rewards, to the welcome bonus:.

    I also put together my list of pros and cons for the Blue Cash Everyday Card:.

    When applying for a credit card, obviously the welcome offer, eligibility rules, and fees, are major considerations. So below I’ll cover the details of that for the Amex Blue Cash Everyday.

    The Amex Blue Cash Everyday is offering the following welcome bonus: You may be eligible for as high as $200 cash back after spending $2,000 in purchases on your upcoming Card in the first 6 months. Welcome offers vary and you may not be eligible for an offer. Cash back is received as Reward Dollars, redeemable for statement credit or for other select options. Terms Apply.

    That’s a reasonable bonus for a no annual fee card, and the spending requirement is low enough that most people should be able to hit it. However, it’s also not that much to get excited about, compared to some of the other welcome offers out there.

    Amex cards tend to be fairly easy to get approved for if you have excellent credit. Here are the main rules to be aware of:.

    Amex also has a pre-application eligibility tool that lets you check whether you’ll be approved for the card without any impact on your credit score. This is worth using if you’re not sure that you’ll qualify.

    The Blue Cash Everyday Card has no annual fee. Not the first year, not ever. That alone makes it worth considering as a long-term card in your wallet, even if it’s not your primary spender.

    Recent findings suggest that holding no annual fee cards long term is also a great way to help your credit score. About 30% of your score comes from credit utilization (the more available credit you have but don’t use, the better), and 15% comes from credit history length (the older your average account age, the better). A no annual fee card you keep open for years helps on both fronts.

    The Blue Cash Everyday Card does have foreign transaction fees (2.7%) (Rates & Fees), so I wouldn’t use it for purchases in foreign currencies. Stick to domestic spending with this one, and find a card with no foreign transaction fees if you’ll be spending time abroad.

    The Amex Blue Cash Everyday has three main bonus categories, each earning 3% cash back on up to $6,000 per year in purchases (then 1%).

    With the Blue Cash Everyday, you earn 3% back at U.S. supermarkets on up to $6,000 per year (then 1%). Earning 3% back at supermarkets with no annual fee is a solid deal, and this is one of the better no annual fee cards for U.S. supermarket spending.

    As with most grocery bonus categories, this generally won’t include warehouse clubs (like Costco), superstores (like Walmart or Target), convenience stores, or discount stores. Traditional supermarkets and grocery chains are what you’re looking for.

    With the Blue Cash Everyday, you also earn 3% back at U.S. gas stations on up to $6,000 per year (then 1%). This is one of the better no annual fee cards for gas station spending.

    This is the bonus category that makes the Blue Cash Everyday stand out from its siblings. You earn 3% back on U.S. online retail purchases on up to $6,000 per year (then 1%). This covers purchases made on a website or app from a U.S. retail merchant that sells physical goods directly to consumers.

    Given how much shopping happens online these days, this can be a really valuable category. You won’t find this bonus on many other cards.

    In a recent development, for purchases outside the bonus categories, you earn 1% cash back. This is where the card falls short. At just 1% on non-bonused spending, you’ll definitely want to pair this with a card that offers a better return on everyday purchases.

    With the Amex Blue Cash Everyday, you earn Reward Dollars that can be redeemed as statement credits at a rate of 1.0 cents per point, and there’s no minimum cash back balance required before you can redeem.

    It’s simple and straightforward, though it’s worth knowing that you can’t use cash back to pay your minimum payment due.

    Industry observers note that benefits and credits can certainly help with justifying holding onto credit cards. In the case of the Amex Blue Cash Everyday, you wouldn’t expect very valuable perks, given the card’s lack of an annual fee. However, it’s an area where I’d say the card actually exceeds expectations, and offers solid value.

    The Blue Cash Everyday offers up to $7 back per month (up to $84 per year) as a statement credit when you use your enrolled Blue Cash Everyday to purchase a subscription, including a bundle subscription, on DisneyPlus.com, Hulu.com, or Stream.ESPN.com U.S. websites, with no minimum purchase requirement. Subscriptions are subject to auto-renewal. If you already pay for any of those services, this is an easy credit to use. (Enrollment required).

    You can also earn up to $15 per month (up to $180 per year) in statement credits when you purchase Home Chef meal solutions online with your Blue Cash Everyday Card. If you use Home Chef, this is a significant benefit. If you don’t, it’s probably not worth signing up just for the credit. (Enrollment required).

    According to recent reports, the Blue Cash Everyday Card also offers 0% intro APR on purchases and balance transfers for 15 months from the date of account opening. After that, the variable APR is at the moment between 19.74% - 28.74% (Rates & Fees).

    Industry observers note that I generally recommend avoiding financing purchases through credit cards. But if a short-term 0% APR opportunity can help you manage a large purchase and you can pay it off before the rate increases, it’s a nice option to have.

    Another card benefit is access to Amex Presale Tickets® and Amex Reserved Tickets®, which can come in handy if you’re trying to score tickets to an in-demand concert or sporting event.

    According to recent reports, every Amex card gives you access to the Amex Offers program, which provides targeted deals with a variety of retailers. Different cards get different offers, so having multiple Amex cards means more chances to save.

    Recent findings suggest that I try to have as many Amex cards as possible specifically to take advantage of this. Having a no annual fee card like this is ideal, since the card isn’t costing you anything, but you’re still getting access to potentially valuable offers.

    The Amex Blue Cash Everyday comes with coverage to protect your rental car when you charge the rental to this card. The coverage applies for eligible damage or theft, and it’s secondary, so it kicks in after your own car insurance. There are some exclusions, and it doesn’t include liability coverage, so check your card benefits guide for the full details.

    Car rental loss and damage insurance: Eligibility and Benefit level varies by Card. Terms, Conditions, and Limitations Apply. Please visit americanexpress.com/benefitsguide for more details. Underwritten by AMEX Assurance Firm. Car Rental Loss or Damage Coverage is offered through American Express Travel Related Services Company, Inc.

    Recent findings suggest that the Blue Cash Everyday Card also offers purchase protection of up to $1,000 per covered purchase for up to 90 days from the purchase date. You need to pay with the card in order to take advantage of this coverage.

    The Amex Blue Cash Everyday Card is a solid no annual fee cash back card with useful bonus categories at supermarkets, gas stations, and online retailers. The 3% rate in those categories is strong for a no annual fee card, and the Disney streaming credits, Home Chef credits, and Amex Offers add extra value on top.

    While there are several reasons to consider the Blue Cash Everyday Card, there are also a couple of alternatives that I think are better for most people.

    Sources indicate that if you generally like the idea of the Blue Cash Everyday Card, there might still be a better play here. The Blue Cash Preferred® Card from American Express (learn more) is the premium version of the card, and it could be worth applying for it instead (Enrollment is required for select benefits).

    It has been revealed that the major question is whether the Preferred’s $0 intro annual fee for the first year, then $95. annual fee (Rates & Fees) is worth the upgrade. If you spend at least $267 per month at U.S. supermarkets, the extra 3% (the Preferred earns 6% cash back at U.S. supermarkets on up to $6,000 per year in purchases, then 1%) on groceries alone will cover the fee. The Preferred also adds 6% cash back on select U.S. streaming and 3% on transit, which the Everyday doesn’t offer.

    On the flip side, the Everyday has two things the Preferred doesn’t: 3% on U.S. online retail purchases and a 0% intro APR offer. If you do a lot of online shopping and not as much grocery shopping, the Everyday could be the better card.

    One nice thing is that you could start with the Blue Cash Preferred (with a $0 intro annual fee for the first year, then $95.), and if the math doesn’t work out, downgrade to the Blue Cash Everyday after year one. That way you get the bigger welcome bonus and can test the higher earning rates.

    While there are lots to like about the Blue Cash Everyday, it’s also not particularly well-rounded if you’re looking for an all-in-one cash back credit card.

    The card offers 3% cash back at U.S. supermarkets, U.S. gas stations, and U.S. online retail purchases (up to certain limits), but on other purchases you’ll earn 1% cash back.

    Industry observers note that everyone will have to crunch the numbers for themselves, but 1% cash back is pretty uncompetitive nowadays for savvy consumers. For example, the no annual fee Citi Double Cash® Card (learn more) offers 1% cash back when you make a purchase, and 1% cash back when you pay for that purchase (in the form of ThankYou points).

    The Blue Cash Everyday wins in its bonus categories, earning 3% at supermarkets, gas stations, and online retailers compared to the Double Cash’s flat 2%. But the Double Cash wins everywhere else, earning 2% on all purchases versus just 1%.

    If your spending is heavily concentrated in supermarkets, gas, and online shopping, the Blue Cash Everyday will earn you more. If your spending is more spread out across lots of different categories, the Double Cash’s flat 2% on everything will likely come out ahead.

    The Double Cash also has a major advantage in flexibility. Its ThankYou points can be transferred to airline and hotel partners (in conjunction with a premium Citi card like the Citi Strata Premier® Card), giving those points the potential to be worth well more than 2 cents each. The Blue Cash Everyday’s rewards are purely cash back.

    The ideal setup? Have both. Use the Blue Cash Everyday for supermarkets, gas, and online retail where it earns 3%, and the Double Cash for everything else at 2%.

    I think the Blue Cash Everyday is a very decent cash back card with bonus categories most spenders can take advantage of. The card’s main weakness is the 1% rate on everything outside the bonus categories — and even on those categories once you reach the annual cap. For that reason, I’d recommend pairing it with a flat-rate card like the Citi Double Cash (2% on everything) to fill in the gaps. Together, they make a simple, effective, no annual fee credit card cash back setup.

    It has been revealed that if you find yourself spending more at supermarkets over time, you can always upgrade to the Blue Cash Preferred for that 6% supermarket rate. But for a no annual fee, low-maintenance starting point, the Blue Cash Everyday is a great choice.

    Lufthansa Management Threatens To Massively Shrink Airline, Lay Off Employees

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1809 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that lufthansa is the “flagship” airline of Lufthansa Group, yet somehow, is the least profitable airline in the whole organization.
    • Industry observers note that unfortunately things haven’t turned out so great.
    • Well, Lufthansa pilots are just days from possibly being able to strike again, no agreement has been reached for long term peace with employees, and management is threatening to massively shrink its mainline operation.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that lufthansa is the “flagship” airline of Lufthansa Group, yet somehow, is the least profitable airline in the whole organization. 2026 was supposed to be an exciting turnaround year for Lufthansa, as it’s even the carrier’s 100th anniversary.

    Industry observers note that unfortunately things haven’t turned out so great. Earlier this year, the carrier dealt with massive labor problems, and back-to-back-to-back strikes. Just a few months ago, the firm’s senior management claimed it wanted to turn over a new leaf with labor relations, and stop fighting with employees, so that it could find long term solutions.

    How is that working out? Well, Lufthansa pilots are just days from possibly being able to strike again, no agreement has been reached for long term peace with employees, and management is threatening to massively shrink its mainline operation. In other words, it’s just another day at Lufthansa!

    Industry observers note that lufthansa and its pilots have been in negotiations for quite some time over the future of the company. As you’d expect, broadly speaking, negotiations revolve around pay and future flying opportunities. As you’d expect at any airline, employees want as much flying as possible, and as substantial of a fleet as possible, since that’s what maximizes their compensation.

    The matter with Lufthansa Group management is that the tech giant’s solution to everything is to simply create new, low cost subsidiaries. And if Lufthansa Group management doesn’t like the terms with its subsidiaries, then it just shuts down the subsidiaries and creates new ones.

    Industry observers note that so that brings us to the current issue. Essentially, Lufthansa’s problem is that the airline doesn’t make money on short haul flights, given high costs and intense competition. So we’ve seen the carrier increasingly outsourcing this flying to Lufthansa City Airlines, a subsidiary with lower operating costs, operating the same kinds of planes as you’ll see in the mainline fleet.

    According to recent reports, lufthansa is asking its pilots to accept wage freezes, and is promising a certain level of career development opportunities. Pilots aren’t happy with what’s being proposed, so what’s Lufthansa’s solution?

    Management is reportedly proposing a new initiative to the supervisory board, which would see the core Lufthansa brand massively reduce its regional flying, and largely outsource this to lower cost operations, like Lufthansa City Airlines. The idea would be to make Lufthansa primarily a long haul airline, and then have much of the short haul flying be operated by a subsidiary.

    Lufthansa’s mainline fleet presently consists of 260+ planes, with another 120+ planes on order. One proposal would see the mainline fleet reduced to 100 long haul aircraft and 100 short haul aircraft, with other planes being assigned to Lufthansa City Airlines.

    One radical proposal could even see Lufthansa exclusively have a long haul fleet and ditch short haul flying, though it’s noted that this isn’t the most likely scenario, and it could take several years for something like that to be implemented.

    It has been revealed that keep in mind that going back to 2017, Lufthansa had guaranteed pilots a minimum fleet size of 325 aircraft, but it terminated that agreement at the end of 2021. So it’s really hard for employees to trust any promises by management, when they can just be terminated.

    There’s no denying that labor relations can be incredibly challenging, and that the economics of intra-Europe flying are also tough, when you have competitors like Ryanair, though Lufthansa doesn’t face nearly as much competition on that front as other carriers. Then again, Frankfurt (FRA) and Munich (MUC) aren’t exactly massively leisure destinations either.

    Most airline employees want their manufacturer to succeed, and just want to be compensated fairly. Admittedly economics don’t always align. But what I find incredibly toxic is the approach taken by Lufthansa management. Let’s compare it to a marriage (which I think is a fair way to view the relationship between management and employees, since they’re “stuck” with one another).

    Lufthansa’s approach is to constantly threaten employees by saying that “if you don’t do what we want, we’ll just get rid of you.” That’s simply not a good faith way to approach things. Why would Lufthansa employees trust management, when they’ve repeatedly torn up contracts, and shown employees they simply don’t care? It would be like threatening to leave your spouse every time you have an concern, rather than trying to find a solution.

    Sources indicate that nothing against Lufthansa Group CEO Carsten Spohr personally, but I don’t understand how the board thinks he’s the best person for the job. Where’s the accountability for the endless management mistakes that have horribly impacted Lufthansa’s bottom line? Lufthansa’s employees are paying the price for the lack of success that comes as a result of all of Lufthansa’s errors, from the botched Allegris rollout, to Lufthansa’s very bad luck with new aircraft orders.

    It has been revealed that and before anyone notes “oh, but the unions,” contrast what has happened at Lufthansa Group to what has happened at Air France-KLM, under the leadership of Ben Smith. Smith has now been CEO at Air France for over eight years, and there hasn’t been a single strike under his leadership. Under the previous Air France-KLM CEO, there were endless strikes, and the situation got so bad that senior executives were being chased up a fence and having their clothes ripped off.

    Recent findings suggest that this highlights that good labor relations absolutely can happen, balancing the needs of employees and the firm. But it requires showing employees that you actually care about the company and their future. What was one of Smith’s first orders of business when he took the job at Air France-KLM? He eliminated Joon, the low cost carrier at the airline that was supposed to basically be a labor arbitrage opportunity. That was a way to show employees how much he respected them, and that he wanted a fair agreement, rather than one that would undermine them.

    In a recent development, meanwhile Spohr’s solution to literally everything is to just threaten to start latest subsidiaries or shut down existing subsidiaries. The irony is that Spohr started his career as a pilot, so you’d think he’d have respect for employees, having been on the other side. But clearly once he became senior management, his love for aviation turned into disdain for employees.

    A few months ago, Lufthansa management claimed it wanted to turn over a new leaf when it comes to labor relations. That didn’t last long, because now the airline is back to its “do what we say or we’ll create a new subsidiary” approach.

    I don’t have a strong opinion on the exact negotiations as such. Obviously it’s a tough time for aviation, and intra-Europe flying is challenging. But if you ask me, the toxicity that has been created by Lufthansa management due to the lack of good faith negotiations just can’t be undone.

    If your only solution to everything is “oh, we’ll create a new subsidiary,” and if that doesn’t work, maybe it’s time for a new strategy. The fact that American CEO Robert Isom and Lufthansa Group CEO Carsten Spohr still have their jobs are two of the industry’s greatest mysteries.

    What do you make of Lufthansa’s latest threat to employees?

    #134116. Industry News: Is Qantas Really Replacing Its Boeing 737-800s With Airbus A321XLRs Built For Longer Routes?

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1501 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Simpleflying ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Is Qantas Really Replacing Its Boeing 737-800s With Airbus A321XLRs Built For Longer Routes?

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1501 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Is Qantas really replacing its Boeing 737-800s with Airbus A321XLRs built for longer routes?
    • That transition sits inside Project Winton, Qantas' fleet renewal program that leads a decisive pivot from Boeing narrowbodies toward Airbus aircraft alongside Airbus A220s for QantasLink.
    • Qantas is replacing its Boeing 737-800s with the Airbus A321XLR, even though the vast majority of its A321XLRs fly domestic sectors rather than the long-range missions the aircraft was designed to serve.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Is Qantas really replacing its Boeing 737-800s with Airbus A321XLRs built for longer routes? For travelers across Australia and beyond, such a decision greatly impacts how Qantas prepares to run its busiest domestic corridors and regional gateways over the next decade. The airline's 737 fleet carries nearly half of all passengers Qantas flies each year, so any shift in the aircraft replacing those jets carries major consequences for flight frequency, onboard comfort, and airline profitability.

    That transition sits inside Project Winton, Qantas' fleet renewal program that leads a decisive pivot from Boeing narrowbodies toward Airbus aircraft alongside Airbus A220s for QantasLink. So what is Qantas planning, and how could this move set the airline up for a decade of dominance?

    Qantas is replacing its Boeing 737-800s with the Airbus A321XLR, even though the vast majority of its A321XLRs fly domestic sectors rather than the long-range missions the aircraft was designed to serve. Instead of reserving the extra-long-range narrowbody strictly for distant international flying, Qantas is leaning on the A321XLR as its main high-capacity domestic replacement for its aging 737-800 fleet across Australia's busiest trunk corridors.

    Qantas' commitment to the A321XLR expanded steadily as fleet renewal requirements evolved. What started as an initial proposal for at least 20 A321XLRs grew to 28 aircraft, and in August 2025 Qantas ordered 20 more A321XLRs to accelerate 737 retirements, bringing its total A321XLR order to 48 jets. Stepping up the order count gives Qantas deeper replacement capacity as older single-aisle airframes reach retirement age, and demand remains strong across major domestic city pairs.

    It has been revealed that deliveries and early fleet withdrawals have already moved into active operations. Qantas took six A321XLRs during its 2026 financial year ahead of 737 fleet retirements beginning in late 2026, while signing a seven-year agreement to sell 44 737-800s and 88 CFM56-7B engines to AerFin, with initial aircraft exits already underway in late 2026, as per AeroMorning. Together, early arrivals and initial retirements mark the start of a multi-year transition away from Qantas' Boeing narrowbody base.

    Inside Project Winton, a name drawn from Winton, Queensland, where Qantas was founded in 1920, the airline is pairing A321XLRs at the mainline level with Airbus A220s, including A220-300s, for QantasLink to modernize its narrowbody operations across different route tiers. Unlike most other operators that use the A321XLR purely as a long-range specialty jet, Qantas is aligning its capacity growth with how demand behaves across both major domestic city pairs and thinner regional or international links.

    Passenger volume and financial upside sit right at the center of that calculus. The reality for Qantas is that the 737 fleet carries nearly half of all passengers the airline flies each year, so upgrading that core segment of the fleet directly affects everyday schedule reliability, seat capacity, and unit economics across high-frequency domestic flying. Replacing 737-800s with A321XLRs and A220-300s is also projected to add between AUD 150 million and AUD 200 million per year to earnings by 2027, as reported by Simple Flying, which gives Qantas a clear financial incentive to push forward with the transition even when many XLRs fly domestic sectors.

    Range and route versatility add another layer to how Qantas weighs the decision. While the A321XLR offers up to 5,400 miles (8,700 km) of range, roughly 1,864 miles (3,000 km) farther than the 737, Qantas does not need to fly every single A321XLR at maximum range to get value out of the airframe. Having extra range and cabin capacity in reserve lets the airline deploy the same aircraft type across busy domestic trunks and keep the option open for longer domestic sectors and selected regional international routes as demand warrants.

    In a recent development, from Qantas' perspective, the A321XLR is about network flexibility and opening markets that current narrowbodies cannot serve reliably. Qantas Group CEO Vanessa Hudson has emphasized that the extra-long-range narrowbody gives the airline flexibility to reach destinations its current narrowbody fleet cannot, pairing domestic workhorse duties with international options such as the scheduled Brisbane–Manila service, as noted by Airliner World. For an airline operating across vast Australian distances and regional Asian markets, having range in reserve lets Qantas adapt schedules, no longer having to commit widebodies to thinner routes.

    According to recent reports, outside observers, however, read the aircraft's role in different ways, some with enthusiasm and others with skepticism. Enthusiasts and frequent-flyer commentators, including voices on One Mile At A Time and r/QantasAirways, often view the A321XLR as a practical, high-capacity narrowbody alternative that upgrades single-aisle comfort and capacity on busy domestic and regional hops. By contrast, Analytic Flying has floated a different theory suggesting cargo capability played a role in the selection, an argument that remains speculative rather than Qantas' stated rationale, especially because adding a Rear Center Tank for extra fuel reduces underfloor cargo volume compared with a standard A321neo.

    Those differing viewpoints highlight why the A321XLR has drawn so much attention in aviation circles. Qantas is treating long-range capability as a strategic buffer for route flexibility and network growth, whereas outside analysts test every angle of the economics, from payload and fuel-tank trade-offs to whether a domestic-heavy fleet needs extra range on every flight.

    Sources indicate that choosing the Airbus A321XLR over other narrowbody and cabin options comes down to how Qantas manages seat density, onboard comfort, and range headroom with a range of different flying profiles. Selecting an extended-range Airbus narrowbody over a standard 737-sized replacement, like the MAX, gives Qantas a single airframe family with higher passenger capacity and longer-sector reach than a baseline 737-800, meaning that capacity can be properly matched on a route-by-route basis.

    Sources indicate that inside the A321XLR subfleet itself, Qantas is splitting cabin layouts rather than forcing one interior onto every flight. Early domestic-configured A321XLRs pack 197 or 200 seats, including 20 recliner business seats, to maximize capacity on high-demand routes, while 16 A321XLRs scheduled from 2028 introduce lie-flat business suites with sliding doors and 19-inch (48 cm) screens for longer domestic and international sectors.

    Contrasting domestic trunk flying against pure long-haul deployment also reveals why Qantas' approach stands apart from airlines using the A321XLR mainly for thin international routes. Across the industry, the overall consensus, as noted by Cirium, is to reserve the XLR for distant international routes, but Qantas flies most of them on busy domestic routes, keeping range in reserve for longer domestic and international sectors. That trade-off means domestic flyers on early XLRs get recliner seats rather than lie-flat beds, making route-matched tiering central to the strategy.

    According to recent reports, replacing all of the 737-800s with A321XLRs is not an overnight swap or a risk-free transition, and several caveats and operational risks shape how the fleet shift unfolds on the ground. 737-800 retirements are rolling out gradually rather than all at once, under Qantas' seven-year sale agreement covering 44 737-800s and 88 CFM56-7B engines with aftermarket specialist AerFin, initial exits are starting in late 2026 with 9 more planned for 2027, and select remaining 737-800s are slated for cabin refurbishments from 2027 to keep older frames competitive during the multi-year handover.

    Sources indicate that cabin layout adjustments and route schedule shifts also test how swiftly the newly introduced narrowbody settles into everyday service. As reported by Simple Flying, early A321XLR deliveries drew scrutiny over economy washroom ratios before Qantas added a third economy lavatory, trimming seat count by 3 seats from the fourth aircraft onward and planning retrofits for the earliest jets. Additionally, the A321XLR's international debut on Brisbane–Manila shifted from October 25, 2026, to February 1, 2027, leaving Airbus A330-200s on the route in the meantime.

    Finally, delivery timing and supply-chain exposure are still very real variables for Qantas' fleet planners. Because Qantas built flexibility into its retirement schedule in case A321XLR deliveries slip, any ongoing manufacturing or supply-chain bottlenecks could keep older 737-800s, or interim widebody assignments, in service longer than initially hoped, making disciplined delivery progression essential as the transition begins to mature.

    Recent findings suggest that the bottom line is straightforward because Qantas is genuinely replacing its 737-800s with the A321XLR, using a long-range narrowbody primarily to support its high-demand domestic flying while still keeping extra range in reserve for longer domestic and international routes. For Qantas, the A321XLR is not an all-or-nothing long-haul specialist, and is adapting the jet to Australia's busiest single-aisle corridors and pacing the transition over several years.

    Recent findings suggest that for passengers and industry watchers alike, what matters next is how smoothly deliveries, cabin configurations, and route schedules come together across the late 2020s and how that will affect the airline's prepares. With initial 737-800 exits underway, the Brisbane–Manila A321XLR launch set for February 1, 2027, and lie-flat business suite frames scheduled to arrive from 2028, Qantas' narrowbody fleet will look quite a lot different by the end of the decade, even as some 737-800s still remain part of the picture along the way.

    For me, the logic of picking up this card is pretty straightforward, and I’ve shared that in much more detail.     On the most basic level, that Bilt Cash earns me 1x points per dollar spent on my housing payments (without any sort of fee), plus I take advantage of the Points Accelerator feature, which earns me an extra 1x points per dollar spent up to five times per year, by redeeming $200 in Bilt Cash.     It has been revealed that as I’ve covered, changes are coming to Bilt as of 2027. While the changes are being made in the name of “simplifying” things, I’d argue that it only creates even more complexity, at least for existing members. Essentially, starting in 2027, Bilt members will earn points for their housing payment as a percentage of their card spending, in lieu of earning 4% back in Bilt Cash on all their spending.

    Industry observers note that the good news is that through December 31, 2026, you can still opt into the old system for being rewarded, and that will then be honored in 2027 and beyond.     LATAM Airlines unveils new A321XLR cabins with eye on US expansion

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (343 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thepointsguy

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The next frontier for the Airbus A321XLR is South America.
    • Recent findings suggest that after opening dozens of fresh transatlantic routes, the long-range narrow-body will make its debut with LATAM Airlines in March 2027.
    • LATAM, a close partner of Delta Air Lines, will outfit its fleet of XLRs with 174 seats.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The next frontier for the Airbus A321XLR is South America.

    Recent findings suggest that after opening dozens of fresh transatlantic routes, the long-range narrow-body will make its debut with LATAM Airlines in March 2027. The airline has yet to say which routes the XLRs will fly, but executives have previously outlined opportunities to connect the U.S. and South America.

    LATAM, a close partner of Delta Air Lines, will outfit its fleet of XLRs with 174 seats. Business class will feature 12 lie-flat suites supplied by Thompson Aero Seating in a 1-1 layout with privacy doors.

    The suites include 19-inch personal entertainment screens, Bluetooth connectivity and in-seat charging options.

    Economy features 13-inch screens at each of the 126 seats, which are supplied by Recaro, plus Bluetooth connectivity and USB-C outlets. The cabin includes 36 extra-legroom seats.

    Sources indicate that “The Airbus A321XLR allows us to take our value proposition to the next level and elevate the travel experience for our passengers,” said Paulo Miranda, the chief customer officer of LATAM, in a statement. He described the interior, which features red, orange and blue hues, as “inspired by South America.”.

    It has been revealed that LATAM executives have said it could fly the XLR on routes into the U.S. from its hub at Jorge Chavez International Airport (LIM) in Lima. However, those intends were called into question in May over the addition of a "connection fee" at LIM.

    In a recent development, the airline and Delta serve six U.S. destinations from LIM: Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL), Los Angeles International Airport (LAX), Miami International Airport (MIA), John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK), Orlando International Airport (MCO) and, since January 2026, Salt Lake City International Airport (SLC).

    LATAM did not comment on specific route prepares for the XLR.

    The XLR is the second latest airplane type for LATAM in as many years. The airline took delivery of its first Embraer E195-E2 in October. It will use the small jet to expand its feeder network in Brazil and support additional long-haul, intercontinental flying.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Rep.-elect Chris Rabb, D-Pa., greets current members of Congress in the Capitol on Nov. 11. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    When Rep.-elect Chris Rabb first worked on Capitol Hill in the 1990s, it didn’t exactly inspire him to want to go into politics.

    “I remarked, ‘Oh, this is how the sausage is made? I should be a vegan,’” the Pennsylvania Democrat recalled.

    Industry observers note that working for Carol Moseley Braun, the first Black woman elected as a U.S. senator, Rabb saw threats and “just vile things” directed at her.

    “My entrée to service behind the scenes was seeing voluminous amounts of violence, hate speech and death threats against my boss, and I thought to myself, ‘Why would anyone want to serve?’” he said.

    During his time in the state legislature starting in 2017, Rabb “fell in love with public service, despite the vitriol.” Now, the democratic socialist describes coming to Congress as “surreal,” as he succeeds retiring Rep. Dwight Evans in a deep-blue district based in West Philadelphia.

    Rabb is one of more than a dozen incoming members who have worked on the Hill before, ranging from interns to chiefs of staff and everything in between.

    In a recent development, unlike some in the 100-plus-strong freshman class, they already know their way around the hallways. And Rabb has some advice for his new colleagues: “Treat your staff well. Take care of your staff; they’ll take care of you.”.

    Here are some of the former staffers who will join the House in January.

    A couple years ago, Killin was working as chief of staff to former second gentleman Doug Emhoff. But she started out on the Hill.

    “It is helpful to know, as I joke, where the bathrooms are, but I still feel like I have a lot to learn,” remarked the Army veteran, who unseated Republican Rep. Jeff Crank in a Colorado Springs-area district.

    She served as the top staffer for three House Democrats: Donna Shalala of Florida, Carolyn Maloney of Latest York and Marie Gluesenkamp Perez of Washington.

    “I’ve actually opened up two freshman offices, so it’s helpful to have done that before,” Killin said.

    White will be just the third person in modern times to hold the job of nonvoting D.C. delegate. He replaces retiring Del. Eleanor Holmes Norton — also his former boss.

    Sources indicate that before his time on the D.C. Council, he worked as her legislative counsel, watching her navigate a role with limited power in her perennial fight for statehood.

    “I need to make sure I’m developing a national profile for this seat,” he said, vowing to continue the quest for full representation even as President Donald Trump seeks to exert more control over the District.

    One of just a few Republican women in the freshman class, Gruters said she “never in a million years” imagined coming to Congress herself, despite her years as a staffer.

    Recent findings suggest that she will replace retiring Rep. Vern Buchanan in Florida’s 16th District, after once serving as his operations director. She also worked as district director for Rep. Greg Steube, R-Fla.

    “I never thought this would be the path, but I’m honored to do it,” remarked Gruters, whose husband leads the Republican National Committee.

    Rogers added another title to his résumé last week: freshman class president.

    Industry observers note that his fellow incoming Republicans tapped him for the role. Not so long ago, he was working for the Senate Judiciary Committee, fresh off a stint at the white-shoe law firm White & Case.

    Industry observers note that in 2025 he served as general counsel for Sen. Rick Scott, R-Fla., and plans to keep pushing for a bill he helped draft that aims to crack down on foreign surrogacy contracts. “We are right now selling American children to China, our No. 1 adversary,” Rogers mentioned, describing it as “deplorable.”.

    It has been revealed that rogers will succeed retiring GOP Rep. Neal Dunn in the Florida Panhandle.

    García’s run for her boss’s seat drew controversy from the start. When Rep. Jesús “Chuy” García, D-Ill., waited to publicly announce his retirement until after the filing deadline in Illinois had already passed, critics blasted him for effectively boxing out other candidates and clearing the way for his chief of staff.

    He faced a rare formal disapproval vote in the House over the move. But García has insisted she is more than a hand-picked successor, saying on her campaign website that she has “delivered solutions rooted in lived experience.”.

    The son of Ghanaian immigrants, Boafo is a state delegate who has lobbied on the Hill for tech company Oracle.

    He also worked as campaign manager for Rep. Steny H. Hoyer, earning an endorsement from the retiring longtime Democrat and campaign cash from groups aligned with him.

    Boafo prevailed in a crowded primary, even as Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi threw her weight behind a different candidate, former Capitol Police officer Harry Dunn.

    Sell worked under then-House Agriculture Chair Larry Combest during the 2000 crop insurance overhaul and the fight over the 2002 farm bill. He later joined his former boss in launching an agricultural lobbying firm, Combest, Sell and Associates.

    Once a precocious child magician who wrote his own book of tricks, Lasher also got an early start in politics.

    “I feel supremely fortunate to have wandered into Jerry Nadler’s political orbit as a teenager 30 years ago, and then to have worked in his congressional office a decade later,” Lasher wrote in an opinion piece for City & State New York.

    Sources indicate that backed by the retiring Nadler, the self-described “nerd” beat out a couple of significant names in the primary, including a Kennedy family heir. Another former boss endorsed him, too: Gov. Kathy Hochul. Before serving as a Fresh York state assemblyman, Lasher worked as her policy director.

    Villegas ousted GOP Rep. David Valadao in a closely watched race in the San Joaquin Valley.

    A decade ago, he was an intern for Rep. John Garamendi, D-Calif. And the progressive also interned for former California state Rep. Rudy Salas, who made unsuccessful bids to unseat Valadao in 2022 and 2024.

    In a recent development, A San Diego City councilmember, Von Wilpert flipped the seat held by Republican Rep. Darrell Issa, who decided not to run for reelection under a map redrawn by Democrats.

    Industry observers note that when she worked for the National Labor Relations Board in 2016, she was detailed to the House Education and Labor Committee, working under ranking member Robert C. Scott, D-Va.

    Jackie Wang and Nick Eskow contributed to this report.

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • There’s no denying that AI holds a lot of potential to transform how we go about our every day life, both for better or worse.
    • People are increasingly using AI for travel planning, but here’s an interesting twist on that.
    • An Instagram user with 1.5 million followers who promises to help people master AI has just published a video about how “ChatGPT upgraded me to first class.” Now, that’s not as exciting as it sounds on the surface.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    There’s no denying that AI holds a lot of potential to transform how we go about our every day life, both for better or worse.

    People are increasingly using AI for travel planning, but here’s an interesting twist on that. Can AI help you find award flights and secure upgrades? It’s something I’d like to study in a bit more detail and write about in the coming weeks, but I just saw a post on Instagram that piqued my interest, so I figured it would make for a fun story. Consider this just a little teaser, for the time being.

    An Instagram user with 1.5 million followers who promises to help people master AI has just published a video about how “ChatGPT upgraded me to first class.” Now, that’s not as exciting as it sounds on the surface. The idea is simply that ChatGPT helped someone secure an upgrade through the standard means — it’s not like ChatGPT used his/her/their charm to sweet talk someone into an upgrade by dressing up nicely. 😉.

    Let me actually just quote the description of the video, which covers most of the content:.

    What happens when you ask ChatGPT to upgrade your flight to first class?

    I tried this on my flight in two weeks and it actually worked.

    Go to ChatGPT and switch from Chat to Work at the top. Start a new chat and give it your airline and confirmation code.

    Prompt 1:“Ask me every question you need about my credit cards, my miles, and my memberships, and map out every upgrade currency I own for this exact flight.”.

    ChatGPT shows you that you’ve been sitting on upgrade power this whole time without even knowing it.

    Prompt 2:“Now look up my exact flight, check how empty the first class cabin is, and tell me every way I can get up there, ranked from free to cheapest.”.

    Prompt 3:“Now go get me the upgrade. Use my miles if the math is worth it, and place the upgrade bid at the smartest number, or get me on the upgrade list right now.”.

    ChatGPT opens its own browser, logs into your airline, and actually chases that seat for you while you sit back and do nothing.

    You can watch the video for yourself below.

    A post shared by Maverick Maltin | AI & ChatGPT (@mavgpt).

    I don’t want to suggest AI isn’t useful, but I’d say that the example given is actually very poor. First of all, let’s be clear about what’s actually going on here. He had booked a business class ticket on American from Los Angeles (LAX) to London (LHR), and then upgraded to first class.

    Now, in the first place, something isn’t fully accurate here:.

    Okay, maybe he edited the dates, or something, which is fine, and it’s besides the point, but as a detail oriented airline nerd, I couldn’t help but notice those things. Anyway, let’s assume this is all accurate:.

    To me, this is kind of where AI falls flat, and it isn’t the correct way to use it. The prompt was reportedly to “use my miles if the math is worth it, and place the upgrade bid at the smartest number, or get me on the upgrade list right now.” This is where I get confused — you’d think that AI would be able to scour reviews online, and see that American first class isn’t (well, or wasn’t) really viewed as a product that’s worth the premium.

    According to recent reports, if AI were really providing useful advice here, it would’ve recommend waitlisting with the systemwide upgrade, and otherwise recommending the guy save his 70,000 miles, and use them for something else. While there are definitely some strong use cases for AI, I think this is actually a pretty poor showing of what it can do.

    According to recent reports, by the way, keep in mind that under United’s updated contract of carriage, using AI to help service reservations is banned, and could potentially get your ticket canceled. Whether there’s any enforcement of that remains to be seen.

    Industry observers note that while the thought of using AI to score an upgrade might sound great, don’t count on it actually getting you the best deal. An AI whiz claims he has the secret to using AI to upgrade to first class. All AI did was use the instant upgrade offer that was available directly on American’s website, and it didn’t even encourage him to skip the upgrade due to it not being worthwhile, or waitlisting the upgrade with a systemwide upgrade, which is objectively a much better deal than 70,000 miles.

    What do you make of this AI “assistance” for a first class upgrade?

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that an Alaska Airlines flight was delayed by hours after masked ICE agents stormed the jet bridge of a departing flight to arrest a Mexican national who allegedly had a work permit had overstayed his visa (you know, “the worst of the worst”). This ended up turning into a huge jet bridge melee, leading to additional arrests, as ICE claims that someone hurled hot coffee at the officers.

    In the end, the flight was delayed by hours, as the crew was no longer fit to fly, and the Port of Seattle is outraged. This is quite the story, as flagged by PYOK.

    This incident happened on the morning of Saturday, November 21, 2026, and involves Alaska Airlines flight AS1306, scheduled to operate from Seattle (SEA) to Los Angeles (LAX).

    This was first reported by a passenger on the flight, who explained that “ICE agents just arrested multiple people at SeaTac Airport inside the jet bridge as we were all boarding,” and went on to explain that they were “deplaning because the crew is being replaced due to poor morale.”.

    ICE agents just arrested multiple people at SeaTac Airport inside the jet bridge as we were all boarding. Now deplaning because the crew is being replaced due to poor morale @CNN @nytimes @seattletimes.

    Video taken from the jet bridge demonstrates masked ICE agents trying to arrest people on the jet bridge.

    Sources indicate that masked ICE agents detained two people on a crowded airport jet bridge in Seattle as passengers were boarding a flight. Alaska Airlines said ICE officers gave them no advance notice of the operation. pic.twitter.com/r44WPTvGdv.

    As a result of this incident, the Alaska flight ended up being delayed by hours. It was initially supposed to depart at 8:10AM and arrive at 11:01AM, but instead, departed at 11:03AM and arrived at 1:36PM.

    Here’s how ICE explained its actions:.

    It has been revealed that on November 21, 2026, at approximately 8:05 a.m. PST, ICE officers conducted a targeted enforcement operation to arrest Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, an illegal alien from Mexico who overstayed his visa in violation of our nation’s laws.

    It has been revealed that during the arrest other travelers began to obstruct and assault our law enforcement officers—a federal crime and a felony. One passenger hurled hot coffee on the officers. Other passengers began obstructing federal officers.

    The individual who threw the hot coffee was identified as Sofia Hernandez Mejia, an illegal alien from Mexico and visa overstay. She was subsequently arrested as well. She will be charged with assaulting a federal officer.

    Assaulting and obstructing law enforcement is a crime and a felony. Secretary Mullin has been clear: anyone who assaults or obstructs law enforcement will be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the fullest extent of the law. Our brave law enforcement is facing more than a 1,600% increase in assaults, 3,300% increase in vehicular attacks, and an 8,000% increase in death threats against them. This violence must end.

    On November 21, 2026, at approximately 8:05 a.m. PST, ICE officers conducted a targeted enforcement operation to arrest Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, an illegal alien from Mexico who overstayed his visa in violation of our nation’s laws. During the arrest other travelers began to… https://t.co/nXiBxAqIJ5.

    The Port of Seattle expressed its outrage about the incident, releasing the following statement:.

    In a recent development, we are outraged about this morning’s incident involving ICE and two passengers as travelers boarded AS 1306 to Los Angeles. Immigration enforcement actions at SEA are conducted without the Port’s participation or knowledge. The Port has continually asked, and local federal immigration authorities have previously agreed to protocols at SEA, and we are in conversation with DHS on whether any of these protocols were breached. However, the Port remains committed to the safety of all of our travelers and staff and airline team. This incident was not only distressing for the affected family but the passengers around them, and Port officials continue to engage federal officials to understand more about what occurred.

    Washington Governor Bob Ferguson was also angry, as he held a press conference about what happened, and released the following statement:.

    ICE is completely and totally out of control. Like many Americans, I’m outraged by masked agents, who do not identify themselves, dragging people off jetways as they board a flight, creating chaos in our communities. Today’s actions at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport are just the latest example of ICE’s deeply un-American tactics. I’ll have more to say this afternoon.

    Meanwhile Alaska Airlines took a more toned down approach, and just expressed “concern,” releasing the following statement:.

    We are concerned by this morning’s law enforcement action during the boarding of Alaska Flight 1306. We recognize how distressing this incident has been for employees and guests. Alaska Airlines is required to comply with applicable laws and regulations when interacting with law enforcement officials. We do not direct or coordinate immigration enforcement activity, and we remain committed to protecting the privacy and safety of our guests and employees wherever possible.

    There’s simply no arguing that in terms of public sentiment, the tides have turned in terms of immigration enforcement, with even Trump recently admitting “I think it might be too tough.”.

    Recent findings suggest that Q: You think your deportation policy went too far?Trump: I think it might be too tough. pic.twitter.com/NKhFjZKxnd.

    No matter how you feel about deportations as such, having them go down in this way for someone who simply overstayed their visa is a step too far, in my opinion. I mean, it’s one thing if we’re talking about a violent criminal on some sort of watch list, but that’s clearly not the case here.

    Our four-year-old is currently at the age where he asks “why” in response to everything… and he has a lot of good questions that often make me step back and think “oh, that’s a good point.” I put myself in the situation of being on the jet bridge here as a parent, and trying to explain what was going on.

    Sources indicate that and here’s the thing — it’s one thing if these people were in uniform and identifying themselves, but when you have people who refuse to identify themselves, it’s an especially bad look. It reminds me of another incident we recently saw at Las Vegas Airport (LAS). Like, is this person being robbed in the terminal, or is this an official law enforcement operation?

    A post shared by Chris Motley (@motleymodel).

    Recent findings suggest that on Saturday, an Alaska Airlines flight was delayed by a few hours after ICE agents stormed a jet bridge to arrest someone, leading to a larger fight, which also caused more arrests. It’s one thing if such a disruptive operation were targeting a violent criminal, but is this really the way that someone who overstays a visa should be apprehended?

    The Port of Seattle has expressed outrage over how this was handled, while ICE is outraged at how its “brave law enforcement” is facing increasing violence from the public.

    Industry News: How Much Does It Cost To Fly A Private Jet From Fresh York To California?

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, private jet travel has boomed in popularity since the pandemic, as more people found out how flexible and convenient it was.
    • As such, for high-flying business executives, celebrities, or ultra-high-net-worth individuals, flying privately offers the best experience, especially in the United States, where business jets are a firm feature.
    • In a recent development, one of the most popular destinations for private jets is Los Angeles, so let's use that as a guideline and look at some different options.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, private jet travel has boomed in popularity since the pandemic, as more people found out how flexible and convenient it was. The time saved at airports is considerable, with all the processes streamlined, efficient, and personalized. Private jets are luxurious and very comfortable, as well as saving precious time.

    As such, for high-flying business executives, celebrities, or ultra-high-net-worth individuals, flying privately offers the best experience, especially in the United States, where business jets are a firm feature. Private jet travel can be expensive, but how much does it cost to travel from Latest York to California?

    In a recent development, one of the most popular destinations for private jets is Los Angeles, so let's use that as a guideline and look at some different options. Is there a cheaper way to fly private? Is it cheaper to consider private ownership or charter with an operator on a regular basis? Let's find out!

    Recent findings suggest that in this case, Teterboro Airport (KTEB) in Fresh Jersey is an ideal airport for New York as it is dedicated to business jets and is just 12 miles away from Manhattan. The airport is well-supported with five FBOs available. Van Nuys Airport (KVNY) is the airport of choice for Los Angeles. It is 20 minutes from downtown. The airport sees more than 260,000 movements per year and is one of the busiest private aviation airports in the world.

    According to Air Charter Advisors, chartering a private jet from New York to Los Angeles can start at around $40,000 for a one-way flight on a Cessna Citation Longitude or $50,000 for a heavy jet such as the Bombardier Challenger 604 or Dassault Falcon 2000LXS. Stratos Jets recommends the Bombardier Challenger 300 for this particular trip and estimates a cost of between $34,000 and $41,000 for a one-way flight.

    In a recent development, clay Lacy suggests that a round trip from New York to Los Angeles on a Gulfstream G450 may cost $102,000, and prices include the aircraft, crew, and fuel. Not included in the price are positioning flight time, landing fees, federal excise taxes, or overnight fees. A trip on a light jet between the two cities could cost $56,000, and $79,000 on a mid-size jet.

    Larger and more luxurious jets with more range will command much higher hourly rates than something like a Pilatus PC-12. Of course, the longer the flight, the more fuel is used, and the crew will accrue more hours, adding more to the overall cost. The flight time between Latest York and LA is typically between five and a half and six and a half hours, depending on the aircraft type.

    Sources indicate that private jets are chartered by the hour and can range from $3,500 up to $18,000 per hour. The price varies depending on the type of private jet and its size, as well as many other factors. According to Evojets, the 'ballpark' prices for chartering a private jet and their hourly rate are detailed in the table below.

    Traveling at peak times or during the holidays can also influence the cost of chartering a private jet. If the aircraft needs to be repositioned to pick up the passengers or to return to base, this can result in additional costs. There may also be costs for landing fees or permits, and fuel costs can fluctuate, leading to surcharges. Other extra costs may include crew salary and per diem, accommodation and ground transport costs, and catering.

    Looking at private ownership and operating costs, a pre-owned Gulfstream IV, for example, can be bought for around $3.2 million for an early 1990s model (production ceased in 1992), according to Liberty Jet. The budget needed per year for 200 hours would be $1,668,667. Taking into account the cost of fuel and the aircraft's speed, it equates to an average cost per mile of $19.12.

    Recent findings suggest that if the shortest distance in the air between New York and Los Angeles is 2,446 miles (via a distance calculator), in this case, the flight (one way) would cost $46,767.52 to operate on a Gulfstream IV that flies 200 hours a year. This does not include the initial aircraft cost, just the operating costs, fixed and variable.

    In a recent development, furthermore, Guardian Jet figures are based on 300 operating hours per year, annual fixed costs of $1,070,534, and variable hourly costs of $6,870.20 per hour, meaning that the flight could cost around $62,630. Of course, with private ownership, there are many variables in the equation.

    As such, these figures are only estimated based on the given information and should not be considered fully accurate. There are other alternatives to both private ownership and charter: it all depends on the individual and how much they fly.

    ​​​One option is fractional ownership, where you can buy shares in an aircraft. There are usually 16 shares in an aircraft, and they are based on 800 flying hours a year. Therefore, you can buy 1/16th of an aircraft and acquire 50 flying hours, or 2/16ths for 100 hours, and so on. The cost will vary depending on the aircrafttype. On top of that, there are usually monthly management fees and an occupied hourly fee. All fees are fixed in advance.

    Recent findings suggest that A jet card or membership plan is another option. It works like a pre-paid card, where your flying hours are bought in advance and then used when needed. These are fixed hourly rates that are agreed upon in advance with a broker or operator. Of course, with these and fractional ownership, you have an aircraft at your disposal, without all the costs and hassles of ownership and paying for crew, insurance, hangar, and everything else.

    Empty legs can offer another cheaper alternative to charter. These are when an aircraft is repositioned to return to base without passengers or flying empty to meet passengers somewhere else. Some charter companies will sell these at a highly discounted rate, as much as 50%, 75%, or even 90%, in order to recoup some of the costs. A search on Fly Victor showed that empty legs between Latest York and Los Angeles could be found for the costs detailed in the table above.

    It has been revealed that chartering a private jet offers many advantages and benefits, from flexibility and traveling in comfort and luxury to privacy and time saved, but this does all come at a hefty price. Smaller local airports can be used, therefore avoiding the hassle of large international airports. In this case, Teterboro Airport in New York and Van Nuys Airport in Los Angeles are viable options due to specializing in private jets and being close to the city.

    Industry observers note that to get an accurate quote for a trip between Latest York and Los Angeles, a client should contact a few different charter operators or brokers to compare. It is important to have specific dates in mind, the number of passengers traveling, and any special requirements.

    Industry observers note that this can include catering, special amenities, or celebrating a special occasion. The more details, the better. A charter operator or broker will use this information to calculate the cost, which can vary based on factors like aircraft availability, fuel costs, airport fees, and the duration of your trip.

    Recent findings suggest that each quote will be tailored to the client's exacting needs, based on the aircraft that are available and the current market conditions. If the client travels frequently by private jet, then private ownership is a possibility, but fractional ownership, jet cards, and memberships are also useful to avoid the extra costs and hassles of ownership. Empty legs are a more affordable alternative for a simple one-way charter at a discounted price.

    According to recent reports, when flying regularly between Upcoming York and Los Angeles, there are lots of options and varying prices, so it is important to check and compare for the most competitive price. It is always a good idea to get a few quotes from different brokers and not settle on the first price, unless the client is traveling in an emergency at the last minute.

    Industry News: Zinke PAC gave to family foundation he was investigated for

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1252 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Ryan Zinke, R-Mont., leaves a meeting of the House Republican Conference at the Capitol Hill Club on July 15, 2025.
    • In a recent development, outgoing Montana GOP Rep.
    • Industry observers note that the gift, which has not previously been reported, was made on Aug.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that rep. Ryan Zinke, R-Mont., leaves a meeting of the House Republican Conference at the Capitol Hill Club on July 15, 2025. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    In a recent development, outgoing Montana GOP Rep. Ryan Zinke gave $200,000 in campaign cash to a family foundation headed by his wife that was once at the center of a federal investigation and an ethics scandal that led him to resign as Interior secretary in 2019.

    Industry observers note that the gift, which has not previously been reported, was made on Aug. 31 from Zinke’s leadership political action committee to the nonprofit Great Northern Veterans Peace Foundation, campaign finance records show. The donation is more than the foundation has reported receiving in any year since it was founded nearly two decades ago.

    Zinke’s wife, son, and sister right now serve on its board of directors, according to the foundation’s annual filing with the state of Montana.

    In a recent development, in a brief interview, Zinke denied that any portion of the money transferred to the foundation will directly benefit him or any of his family members who sit on the board of directors. “No, no, never," he noted when asked if any family members will draw a salary from the gift.

    The money will instead go to building a storage barn and kid’s sledding park on the property controlled by the foundation, Zinke remarked.

    None of the records indicate Zinke violated the law or directly benefited from the gift to his foundation.

    “While it's not uncommon for a politician to transfer leftover money from a political war chest to charity, it is pretty rare for a politician to transfer leftover political funds to a charity that they or a relative controls,” mentioned Michael Beckel, director of money in politics reform at Issue One, a bipartisan group that seeks to reduce influence of money in politics.

    Instead, outgoing members typically transfer remaining campaign cash to local party committees or candidates, Beckel added.

    Ethics experts say Zinke’s move highlights ongoing concerns over the broad latitude campaign finance law gives leadership PACs in how they spend money.

    “I definitely think it is something to be concerned about,” said Stuart McPhail, director of campaign finance litigation at Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington, a nonprofit watchdog.

    “Leadership PACs are really nothing more than personal slush funds under today's rules,” he mentioned, noting that unlike regular campaign committees, member leadership PACs are not prohibited from donating to charities or organizations that could directly benefit the member or relative.

    It has been revealed that zinke, a former Navy SEAL who commanded special forces during the Iraq War, converted his traditional campaign committee to a leadership PAC — Commander Zinke Leadership Fund — in March 2026, shortly after announcing he would not run for reelection. It last reported having $1.4 million cash on hand in October of this year.

    It marks the second time one of Zinke’s political committees made a payment to the organization. In 2019, the committee Zinke ran during his earlier years in Congress — he served one term in the House before being tapped as Trump’s first-term Interior secretary — gave over $11,000 to the foundation before winding down operations.

    Recent findings suggest that the Great Northern Veterans Peace Foundation was founded by Zinke and his wife in 2007 in his hometown of Whitefish, Mont., with plans to provide winter recreational activities for children. Its latest tax filing reports revenue of $15,000 and roughly equal expenses in 2024 for snow plowing and park maintenance.

    Zinke’s dealings with the organization were the subject of an ongoing inspector general investigation when he resigned as Interior secretary in January 2019.

    Investigators ultimately did not find that Zinke violated conflict-of-interest laws, but they concluded that he failed to comply with federal ethics obligations and “misused his official position in violation of federal regulations.” The Justice Department declined to prosecute Zinke.

    Industry observers note that zinke stepped down from the foundation in 2017, shortly after his Senate confirmation. But investigators found that he continued to represent the organization in negotiations with the developers of a commercial project adjacent to the foundation’s land and lied to an ethics agent about his involvement in the project.

    The project’s investors included David Lesar, then-chairman of oil services company Halliburton.

    Another Zinke-tied leadership PAC has previously raised eyebrows in Washington.

    Supporting Electing American Leaders PAC — known as SEAL PAC — where Zinke serves as chairman, has been marred by accusations that it funneled money to political consultants instead of candidates. A 2022 CQ Roll Call analysis found that 87 percent of the PAC’s spending went to operating expenses.

    The PAC also made recurring monthly payments to a company registered to Zinke’s son, Wolfgang Zinke, and based at a Zinke family-owned home in Whitefish.

    Sources indicate that SEAL PAC’s executive director, Rob Catron, maintained that the payments constitute a consulting fee to Wolfgang Zinke for management of the PAC website, among other tasks. “He earns every penny of it,” Catron mentioned.

    Recent findings suggest that since May 2022, the PAC has given roughly $270,000 to Wolfgang Zinke’s manufacturer, FG Solutions, for mailing and printing, records show — more than any individual candidate or committee supported by the PAC. The company also received $5,000 from a related super PAC, SEAL PAC USA, which can solicit unlimited contributions for independent expenditures but can’t donate directly to candidates.

    Montana corporate records show Wolfgang Zinke founded FG Solutions – which says it provides services including “personal assistant and any lawful purpose” – just 10 days before it received its first payment from the PAC in 2022.

    Catron defended how the PAC spends money on veterans running for the House, arguing that it takes money to raise money.

    “We raise a lion’s share of our funding through national direct mail fundraising, which is very expensive to do,” he stated, citing the PAC’s use of a national text message fundraising campaign as a major expense.

    Recent findings suggest that SEAL PAC raised about $9.6 million this election cycle, distributing about $1.1 million to GOP lawmakers and candidates, according to Federal Election Commission filings. Most of the committee's funds went to operating expenses, including over $3 million paid to Direct Support Services, a Washington-based vendor, for direct mail postage.

    Zinke’s not the only lawmaker to face scrutiny over how they spent surplus campaign cash in recent years.

    Industry observers note that in 2023, Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., set off alarm bells for transferring $200,000 from his campaign committee to The Sanders Institute, a nonprofit founded by his wife and stepson, following a $350,000 donation from his 2020 presidential campaign coffers.

    The organization briefly shut down during Sanders’ presidential run in 2019 to avoid the appearance of impropriety.

    Sanders’ stepson, David Driscoll — a former executive at Nike and snowboard manufacturer Burton — is listed on the think tank’s website as its executive director, drawing a six-figure annual salary according to tax filings.

    It’s unusual, though not unheard of, for campaign committees to pay family members of the candidate for bona fide work.

    “If [Wolfgang Zinke] is actually performing this work, he’s qualified to do it, and this is his typical market rate for this kind of contract, then it would be permissible, even if this was a campaign account,” McPhail stated about SEAL PAC's payments.

    But the payments could present a legal “gray area” over whether personal-use restrictions apply to certain PACs, according to McPhail.

    The is a cobranded airline card within Atmos Rewards, the joint loyalty program between Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines.

    Some of the best ways to maximize these points include redeeming for premium cabins with Oneworld partners, such as Cathay Pacific and Fiji Airways. However, Atmos Rewards points are also solid for short-haul domestic routes on Alaska Airlines and American Airlines.

That can save $45 per person each way on most itineraries, though the first checked bag still costs $30 on intra-Hawaii flights.

For trips to Hawaii, awards from the West Coast typically start at 12,500 points each way in economy and 30,000 points each way in first class.

    Atmos Rewards is part of the Oneworld alliance, which means you can book partner flights with airlines such as British Airways, Cathay Pacific and Qantas. Keep in mind that partner awards include a $20 nonrefundable booking fee.

    TPG director of travel content Eric Rosen's favorite ways to maximize Atmos Rewards redemptions include booking Cathay Pacific or Japan Airlines business class from the U.S. to Asia for 75,000 points one-way and Fiji Airways business class from the U.S. to Fiji for 75,000 points one-way.
