    Link: Sign-up for a Rakuten account with a best-ever $50 bonus.

    It has been revealed that rakuten is a free online shopping and rewards platform that pays customers either cash back or points for the shopping they do online. Rakuten partners with over 3,500 online retailers, many of which are well known, ranging from Lowe’s, to Nike, to Target. The Rakuten shopping portal concept is simple — if you click through from Rakuten to the partner website, Rakuten tracks the purchase and gets paid a commission, and then you get a reward as well.

    Note that as a consumer, Rakuten is free to use. The commission is paid by the business, so you’ll pay the same price you’d pay if you just went directly to the retailer’s website. To maximize your savings, you can even download the Rakuten browser extension, which will automatically notify you when you can earn extra rewards.

    I should mention that there are several online shopping portals out there to choose from, so Rakuten isn’t the only one. Personally I find that Rakuten is my favorite because it has among the largest selection of partners, it gives you the flexibility to earn cash back or points, and I also find the earnings rates to be very competitive.

    It can always pay to use a site like Cashback Monitor to compare the earnings rates for retailers across portals, so that you’re maximizing your rewards. In some situations you may be better off using other portals, so it’s always worth understanding what your options are.

    According to recent reports, through December 31, 2026, Rakuten is offering a generous elevated refer-a-friend bonus. Specifically, if you refer a friend to Rakuten and they spend $50 within the first 90 days, then both the person referring and the person being referred each receive $50.

    This is truly a best-ever bonus, as we’ve previously only seen a bonus of up to $40 — though admittedly this offer has stuck around for quite some time.

    It has been revealed that this is a very good deal. Essentially Rakuten is giving out $100 total for a $50 purchase, between the person referring and the person being referred. Long term you can potentially get even more value with Rakuten, as rewards can be converted into Amex or Bilt Points.

    Actually earning the $50 Rakuten sign-up bonus is really straightforward:.

    According to recent reports, what’s the timeline with which you’ll actually receive the rewards? With Rakuten you’re paid (either in cash or points) once quarterly, and there’s a cutoff for payments, per the below chart.

    Sources indicate that rakuten partners with literally thousands of retailers, and an eligible purchase worth at least $50 with any eligible retail partner would qualify. When you click over to the partner site, just make sure you keep an eye on any exclusions, since some types of purchases may not qualify for rewards.

    In a recent development, there are also often amazing opportunities to earn up to 100% back or 100x points with select retailers, which is a rate at which I’d gladly buy points all day long, without even factoring in the service being sold. So I take advantage of these deals all the time, even if I don’t actually value the product.

    If you’re not interested in that and don’t have anything you need to buy right now, there’s another creative option. There are easy ways to unlock the $50 bonus, including simply purchasing a $50 gift card through giftcards.com. This is so easy — you can pick up a $50 gift card with a variety of retailers, and then you’ll receive $50 in cash.

    To briefly explain that process, you’d enter giftcards.com in the search bar at the top of Rakuten’s website.

    In a recent development, then click the “Shop Now” button, which will take you to giftcards.com. All your purchases while on that site will automatically be tracked.

    The website sells a variety of gift cards with popular retailers, including DoorDash, Uber, Delta, Southwest, Hulu, Netflix, Dominos, and many more.

    For example, you could buy a $50 DoorDash gift card at face value, and the code will be delivered by email within minutes.

    Once the purchase is complete, you should see Rakuten automatically tracking the purchase.

    Within an hour the purchase should be fully reflected — the Rakuten account will show a credit in the amount of the sign-up bonus, plus the rewards for the actual purchase (which will vary based on whether you choose to earn cash or points). As a standard, giftcards.com offers either 1% cash back, or one point per dollar spent, but sometimes we see increased offers (like right now).

    Taking advantage of this is the obvious choice, in my opinion:.

    In a recent development, the reason that Rakuten is my favorite shopping portal is because Rakuten rewards can be converted into Amex Membership Rewards points or Bilt Rewards points. The exact way this works depends on the currency you choose to earn.

    With the Rakuten and Amex Membership Rewards partnership, you can consistently earn one point in lieu of one cent, assuming you have an Amex card that earns Membership Rewards points. So if a retailer offers 10% cash back, you can instead earn 10x Amex points.

    Based on my latest points valuations, Amex Membership Rewards points are worth 1.7 cents each, because of all the ways there are to redeem the points for first and business class international travel, while getting outsized value. To me that increases the value of the rewards by 70%.

    Sources indicate that this just requires changing one setting in your account, so it’s super easy. The only thing to be aware of is that this points earning opportunity doesn’t apply to the welcome bonus, but does apply to all spending beyond that.

    Industry observers note that that’s not the only opportunity, though. The Rakuten and Bilt Rewards partnership lets members earn Bilt Rewards points in lieu of cash back. Bilt elite members can earn one point in lieu of every one cent, while non-elite members can earn one point in lieu of every two cents. Much like Amex Membership Rewards points, I also value Bilt Rewards points at 1.7 cents each, as there are also many good uses of this points currency.

    What’s cool here is that your cash back can retroactively be converted into Bilt Points for the entire Rakuten “payout” period (roughly quarterly), and that means even the refer-a-friend bonus can be converted into points.

    If you have the choice between one Amex point or one Bilt point, I think many people might prefer the latter, given the value of the rewards, plus how hard they are to earn. However, if the ratio isn’t one point per cent, then I’d go with the Amex partnership instead.

    Beyond the rewards you earn directly with Rakuten, your spending with retailers can of course also earn credit card rewards.

    Rakuten’s co-branded Amex card is among the best cards for Rakuten spending, as it earns 4% cash back on those purchases, on up to $10,000 per calendar year.     💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card is the business credit card of Atmos Rewards, which is the loyalty program of Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines.
    • The card has just undergone a full refresh, and there are many reasons to consider picking up this card, especially if you fly Alaska or Hawaiian with any frequency.
    • Link: Learn more about the Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card is the business credit card of Atmos Rewards, which is the loyalty program of Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines. The card is issued by Bank of America, and is a rebranding of the former Alaska Airlines Visa Business Card.

    The card has just undergone a full refresh, and there are many reasons to consider picking up this card, especially if you fly Alaska or Hawaiian with any frequency. This post is my in-depth Atmos Rewards Business Card review, so I’d like to take a look at the card’s value proposition, for anyone who may be considering applying.

    Link: Learn more about the Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card.

    Before I get into my Atmos Rewards Business Card review, here’s a brief summary of the key details of the card:.

    Below are what I consider to be the pros and cons of the Atmos Rewards Business Card.

    According to recent reports, the Atmos Rewards Business Card is the only business card in the Atmos Rewards ecosystem. To start, let’s cover the welcome bonus, card eligibility rules, annual fee, and more, since these are key factors that cardmembers consider.

    It has been revealed that the Atmos Rewards Business Card is offering a limited time welcome bonus where you’ll get 90,000 bonus points after you make $6,000 or more in purchases within the first 90 days of opening your account. This is the best publicly available bonus that we’ve ever seen on the card, and you can find the bonus offer history in this post.

    In a recent development, based on my latest miles & points valuations, Atmos Rewards points are worth 1.5 cents each, given the great uses of these rewards. That means the 90,000 points are worth $1,350 for me.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card is issued by Bank of America. The good news is that eligibility for this card is unrelated to having any other Atmos Rewards card, so you’re eligible for this card (including the bonus) if you have the Atmos™ Rewards Ascent Visa Signature® credit card (learn more) or Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite® Credit Card (learn more).

    Let me emphasize that you are eligible for this product if you have any of the previously issued personal or business HawaiianMiles Barclays cards, or any of the previously issued personal Alaska Mileage Initiative cards.

    Beyond that, Bank of America doesn’t have many consistent restrictions when it comes to getting approved for business cards. While Bank of America has the 2/3/4 rule and 3/12 rules, those apply to personal cards, and not business cards. Generally those with a Bank of America banking relationship also have the best odds of approval (though it’s by no means a requirement).

    Recent findings suggest that there’s not a consistent credit score you need to have to be approved for this card, though personally I’d hope to have a score in the “good” to “excellent” range, ideally 700+ points. However, people with lower scores have been approved, and people with higher scores have been rejected.

    Applying for this card won’t count as a further card toward Chase’s 5/24 limit, in case that’s a limit you’re trying to stay under.

    I should also mention the following restriction in the terms:.

    I also understand that I may be declined for additional credit card accounts if my business entity at the moment has, or has had, another business card with Bank of America in the preceding 24 month period.

    Recent findings suggest that on the surface, this suggests you may be declined for a Bank of America business card if you have another Bank of America business card. However, anecdotally, this doesn’t appear to be enforced much. I think the term “may” is the key here (which is different than “will”).

    In a recent development, the Atmos Rewards Business Card has a $195 annual fee. That’s on the steep side, though the card does have some premium perks. The good news is that you can add employee cards at no extra cost, so that annual fee covers the cost for all the cards you’ll have.

    Recent findings suggest that the Atmos Rewards Business Card has bonus categories that can help you rack up points faster. Furthermore, spending on the card can help you earn Atmos Rewards elite status. Let’s talk about how rewarding spending on the card can be.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card offers 10x points per dollar spent on flights booked through the Atmos for Business website. If you’re looking to maximize your earning, this is where you want to book your Alaska and Hawaiian flights, as this is an incredible deal.

    You do need your own business to participate in the Atmos for Business program, and once registered, the return on spending is really tough to beat. Based on my valuation of points, that’s like an incremental 15% return on eligible airfare spending, on top of what you otherwise earn.

    Sources indicate that the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers 3x points on all other eligible Alaska and Hawaiian purchases, with no caps. Based on my valuation of Atmos Rewards points, that’s like a 4.5% return on spending. So if you fly either of those Alaska Air Group carriers with any frequency, that’s a solid return on that spending.

    According to recent reports, the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers 2x points on eligible dining purchases. Based on my valuation of Atmos Rewards points, that’s like a 1.5% return on spending. It’s always nice to earn bonus points, though in fairness, 2x points isn’t exactly the biggest return on spending that we’ve seen.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card offers 1x points on all other eligible spending. Based on my valuation of Atmos Rewards points, that’s like a 1.5% return on spending. As you might expect, there are more exciting cards for everyday spending, as independently, that’s not a terribly exciting return.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card can help you earn elite status in the Atmos Rewards program. Specifically, the card offers one status point for every $3 in eligible spending. There’s no cap on how many status points you can earn with the card.

    If you are serious about earning status with spending, I’d recommend instead considering the Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite® Credit Card (learn more), which offers one status point for every $2 in eligible spending.

    Beyond the ability to earn one status point per $3 spent, the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers some additional threshold bonuses for spending, including bonus status points and discount codes:.

    In other words, spending $200,000 per anniversary year would earn you 20,000 bonus status points, plus a discount code for 50% off a base fare. Just to cover the basics of that 50% off base fare discount code, here’s how that works:.

    According to recent reports, so the value of this will depend on how you’d usually travel, but this could easily save you many hundreds of dollars, depending on the type of ticket you book. It’s also still possible to upgrade these tickets, but at least the initial booking has to be in economy.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card also offers a Bank of America relationship bonus. If you have an eligible small business Bank of America checking or savings account, you’ll receive a bonus equal to 10% of the points you earn on each dollar spent.

    This is a way to earn even more rewards, as you’d earn 11x points on Atmos for Business purchases, 3.3x points on Alaska and Hawaiian purchases, 2.2x points on the other purchases eligible for bonus categories, and 1.1x points on everyday spending.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card has no foreign transaction fees, so it’s a decent card to use for purchases abroad, since you can rack up rewards without paying a fee.

    Recent findings suggest that the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers a variety of benefits and credits, which can potentially more than justify the annual fee year after year. These perks are the main reason you want to consider picking up this card, in addition to the great welcome bonus. In no particular order, let’s go over the main benefits.

    According to recent reports, the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers a free checked bag for you and up to six guests on the same reservation when flying on Alaska or Hawaiian. In order to be eligible for this perk, you need to charge the cost of the ticket to your card. Another great thing is that authorized owners on the card can also receive this benefit, as long as their ticket is purchased with the card, so that’s a huge incentive to add authorized users to the card.

    It has been revealed that this is a great benefit that could save you a lot of money — Alaska and Hawaiian ordinarily charge $30-45 per checked bag, so that’s a savings of up to $90 per person roundtrip, if checking bags. If you fly Alaska or Hawaiian fairly often but don’t have elite status, that alone could quickly more than justify the annual fee.

    It has been revealed that the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers preferred boarding for you and up to six guests on the same reservation. In order to be eligible for this perk, you need to charge the cost of the ticket to your card. Another great thing is that authorized consumers on the card can also receive this benefit, as long as their ticket is purchased with the card.

    Industry observers note that this is a valuable benefit that helps you ensure that there’s space in the overhead bin for your bags. It’s also an awesome authorized user perk, so that you can share this benefit with others.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card offers four Alaska Lounge passes annually. The way this works, the primary cardmember will have one Alaska Lounge pass deposited into their Atmos Rewards account at the beginning of the quarter, valid through the end of the quarter.

    Industry observers note that each is valid for access to Alaska Lounges on a single calendar day, in conjunction with a same day flight operated by Alaska, Hawaiian, a oneworld airline, or an Alaska global partner. Each pass is valid for one adult, plus accompanying children. For what it’s worth, a day pass would otherwise cost $60 per person.

    In a recent development, if you’re the primary cardmember on the Atmos Rewards Business Card, you can share your Atmos Rewards points with other members at no cost. The way this works, you can link your accounts with up to 10 other Atmos Rewards members (they don’t have to be family — accounts of friends are fine as well), and then you can move points back and forth for free.

    I’d argue that this is especially compelling for families, because it’s easier to rack up a sizable balance of points when you can consolidate them into one account.

    According to recent reports, the Atmos Rewards Business Card offers 20% back on Alaska and Hawaiian inflight purchases when paying with your card. This applies for the purchase of food, beverages, and Wi-Fi onboard flights, and the statement credit should post to your account within seven days. There’s no limit to how often you can take advantage of this.

    Let me just mention that Alaska and Hawaiian should have free Starlink Wi-Fi fleetwide by some point in 2027, at which point there won’t be savings anymore with Wi-Fi. That being remarked, it can still be used for food and beverages.

    Sources indicate that if you’re the primary cardmember on the Atmos Rewards Business Card, then you’re eligible for a free same day confirmed flight change on Alaska. This ordinarily costs $50 per person, so that’s quite valuable.

    With this, you can change to another flight that might be more convenient, subject to capacity controls. This is especially useful in high frequency markets.

    If you’re the primary cardmember on the Atmos Rewards Business Card, you’re eligible to receive a $50 voucher if you have an Alaska flight that is delayed by at least two hours, or that’s canceled within 24 hours of departure.

    The $50 voucher is valid for 48 hours, and will be delivered to the email address associated with the reservation, and can be used for food, drinks, etc. Travel must have been booked directly with Alaska using the eligible credit card.

    It has been revealed that those with the Atmos Rewards Business Card receive up to a $120 airport security credit every four years, in connection with TSA PreCheck or Global Entry. This is a perk offered by many premium credit cards, and there’s lots of value to this.

    According to recent reports, when talking about an Atmos Rewards credit card, it’s worth acknowledging the general value in earning and redeeming Atmos Rewards points. Alaska & Hawaiian are both in the oneworld alliance, and Atmos Rewards partners not only with oneworld partner airlines, but also with all kinds of other unaligned airlines. I consider Atmos Rewards to be one of the most valuable points currencies out there.

    Sources indicate that atmos Rewards has a distance based award chart, which varies a bit by region. For example, below is the one-way award chart within the Americas.

    I constantly redeem Atmos Rewards points for travel within the United States, particularly on American. For example, all the time I redeem 4,500 points to fly one-way economy from Miami to Tampa (when cash fares would often be $200+), or 15,000 points to fly one-way business class from Miami to Chicago or New York (when cash fares would often be $500+). You simply can’t beat these redemption rates.

    The icing on the cake is that with Atmos Rewards, you earn status points for award flights, so those flights even count toward elite status, and that’s also why I’ve switched my business to Atmos Rewards.

    Of course there are lots of other opportunities with Atmos Rewards points as well. For example, I love the ability to redeem 75,000 points for one-way business class from the United States to many parts of Asia on carriers like Japan Airlines or Starlux Airlines — those are both awards that I’ve booked for myself in the past, and they were a great value.

    It has been revealed that what makes this an even better value is that you can have a free stopover on a one-way award when traveling long haul. One thing worth being aware of is that Atmos Rewards has a $20 per person per direction partner award booking fee. However, that can be waived if you have the Atmos Rewards Summit Card.

    In a recent development, the Atmos Rewards Business Card is the only business card in the Atmos Rewards ecosystem, so how valuable is this product? A few thoughts….

    It has been revealed that first of all, I think there’s a lot of merit to picking up this card for the excellent welcome bonus, which includes a lot of points. The card also has significant ongoing benefits. The card also doesn’t count toward the Chase 5/24 limit, which is nice. Given the value of the Atmos Rewards ecosystem, there’s no reason not to pick up this card, if eligible.

    What about the long term value proposition of the card, though? If you fly Alaska or Hawaiian with any frequency and don’t have elite status, the basic perks add up, including a first checked bag free, preferred boarding, a quarterly lounge pass, free points sharing, and more.

    However, I’d say there’s also merit to picking up one (or both) of the personal Atmos Rewards cards….

    In a recent development, the $395 annual fee Atmos Rewards Summit Card is the most premium Atmos Rewards credit card. While it’s a personal card, I still think it’s worth highlighting, as it’s incredibly lucrative. I’d take it a step further, and say that it’s my favorite airline credit card.

    Among other things, the card racks up status points at the fastest rate, the card allows you to earn Global Companion Awards, offers Alaska Lounge passes, enables free points sharing, waives partner award booking fees, offers 3x points on foreign purchases, and much more.

    If you fly Alaska or Hawaiian with any frequency, then getting this card is an absolute no-brainer. As I see it, the anniversary 25K-point Global Companion Award alone basically justifies the annual fee, and that says nothing of all the other amazing perks.

    According to recent reports, if you’re not set on an Atmos Rewards Business Card but want a dedicated business credit card that’s lucrative, there are some other great options that earn flexible points. Consider these if you want options for redeeming your rewards for more than just on Alaska, Hawaiian, and its partners:.

    Recent findings suggest that the Atmos Rewards Business Card is an excellent business credit card that offers a massive welcome bonus and strong perks. The limited time welcome bonus of 90,000 Atmos Rewards points will come in handy for cardmembers, and is more than enough reason to get the card.

    It has been revealed that if you don’t yet have this card and are eligible, I’d highly recommend applying. This is a card that many people don’t have, yet which offers lots of value and a great bonus.

    Now hiring: Staff to power Democrats’ probes

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1247 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Ranking member Jamie Raskin, D-Md., arrives at the Rayburn Building for a House Judiciary Committee hearing in February.
    • Democrats in Congress have promised to hit the ground running with sprawling oversight investigations in the upcoming year, making the most of their coming majority.
    • Sources indicate that that means staffing up major committees.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Ranking member Jamie Raskin, D-Md., arrives at the Rayburn Building for a House Judiciary Committee hearing in February. He will be a key player in leading oversight efforts next year — and so will Democratic staff. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    Democrats in Congress have promised to hit the ground running with sprawling oversight investigations in the upcoming year, making the most of their coming majority.

    Sources indicate that that means staffing up major committees. And for the dozens of attorneys and other aides preparing to take on a belligerent Trump administration that has cast Democratic oversight as potentially criminal, the job will come with extra scrutiny.

    Arya Hariharan, former chief oversight counsel to Sen. Richard J. Durbin on the Senate Judiciary Committee and now a partner at Holland & Knight, mentioned the pressure will be on from day one.

    “Are you prepared to not sleep very much and know that every single thing you do is going to be scrutinized, every footnote, every comma?” Hariharan said.

    Still, the way Hariharan sees it, serving on the Hill is worth it. “I hope they all fall in love with it because it’s a lovely place to work,” she says of staffers headed there for the first time.

    Industry observers note that the work done by attorneys and other staff in oversight probes can swiftly become part of constitutional law. When Trump adviser Peter Navarro defied a subpoena from Democrats investigating the Jan. 6, 2021, attack on the Capitol, it touched off debates about executive privilege and contempt of Congress. Probes of Hunter Biden led to similar court fights.

    In a recent development, some questions have gone all the way up to the Supreme Court, like in Trump v. Mazars, when the House fought to access Trump’s business records during his first administration in furtherance of toughening up government ethics laws.

    There’s every indication that pressure will continue in the new Congress. James Melendres, a partner at Snell & Wilmer, noted Democrats are poised for aggressive oversight efforts, even if they know it could be tough to make headway against litigation resistant administration officials.

    Recent findings suggest that “Democrats are going to have less than two years to show results. I think they are going to move really fast,” Melendres said.

    Democrats will likely soon start to send out preservation letters to private companies, institutions and others they intend to probe in the new year, if they haven’t already, Melendres said.

    “There may be significant pushback from the administration, from agencies and individual government officials who receive requests. I think third-party, nongovernment agencies and individuals are going to be high on the list for these committees,” he mentioned.

    In addition to the hiring that happens over the next few weeks, House Democrats will have major decisions to make about chamber and committee rules for the new Congress, including who will hold subpoena authority. And off-Hill observers will be watching closely.

    “For companies, for individuals and their counsel, mapping all of that is going to be a substantial part of the job between now and early January,” Melendres said.

    In a recent development, lawmakers need to nail down funding levels for congressional committees and staff — the amount of money involved can make a big difference in how big investigations get. Major committees, and major investigations, take a large amount of staff and expertise to get going.

    It has been revealed that for instance, the special House panel that investigated the Jan. 6 attack on the Capitol spent about $14 million in less than 18 months, including for dozens of staffers.

    Standing committees, such as Oversight and Judiciary, take a good chunk of change, too. In 2025 the House spent $12.9 million on the House Oversight and Government Reform panel, and $13.1 million on the House Judiciary Committee.

    Those expenditures mean dozens of staff working long hours to review documents, send letters, send subpoenas and conduct interviews. Judiciary ranking member Jamie Raskin, D-Md., who is expected to serve as chair next year, said he wouldn’t get into specifics yet about how many resources the upcoming Congress may devote to oversight efforts.

    “But we are talking about the most corrupt administration in the history of the United States, and this is an overwhelming and daunting task that faces us,” Raskin remarked.

    The Trump administration itself has already signaled it intends to push back forcefully on congressional oversight efforts.

    Earlier this month, President Donald Trump described Democrats’ vows to investigate his administration as “extortion at the highest level” and called for the Justice Department to “look into this criminal act, immediately!”.

    Days later, the White House counsel sent a letter saying that subpoena threats from House Oversight ranking member Robert Garcia, D-Calif., and others “may cross the line into blatant criminality.”.

    Industry observers note that U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz for the Southern District of Texas followed up with letters of his own to Sens. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn.; Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass.; and Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., urging them to preserve documents tied to their promised oversight.

    “The American people are entitled to freely associate without their elected officials terrorizing them with aggressive, harassing government action,” Reitz’s letter to Warren said.

    Members of the incoming majority have signaled they intend to defend themselves and their probes, and Blumenthal said he won’t be deterred by the letter.

    “There’s no way that I’m going to be intimidated or bullied. It would be laughable and ludicrous, but it is a clear abuse and misuse of prosecutorial powers and weaponization by the Department of Justice,” remarked Blumenthal, who serves as the top Democrat on the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations.

    As for Raskin, he called the White House counsel letter and other missives “absurd on its face.”.

    It has been revealed that “I’m sure they would love to get into a whole series of letters and counter-letters and litigation. They’re trying to distract everybody from the fact that they just lost the worst landslide electoral repudiation in at least a half century in America, and so they’re going to pick a fight,” Raskin told reporters.

    Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., the likely incoming speaker, told reporters last week that he intended oversight efforts in his chamber to be led by Raskin and Garcia.

    “We haven’t ruled anything in. We haven’t ruled anything out. We’re going to follow the facts. We’re going to apply the law. We’re going to be guided by the Constitution, and we’re going to let the chips fall where they may,” Jeffries remarked.

    Democrats have already publicly listed a handful of job postings for oversight staff and counsel, ranging from the Science to Armed Services to Judiciary panels, set to start early next year.

    Industry observers note that beyond those hires, House Democrats will have to make one major pick they haven’t yet announced — the House counsel. The position, first created in the 1970s, is hired by the majority and advocates for the chamber in court. That attorney, along with a group of bipartisan House leaders controlled by the majority, will steer the chamber’s legal strategy.

    Sources indicate that in prior Democratic Congresses, that office has been active in court; Doug Letter frequently argued on behalf of the Democratic House majority seeking to enforce subpoenas on behalf of congressional committees. The position is held by Matthew Berry in the current Republican-controlled House.

    “I mean, I think a lot of people are interested in that job,” Raskin said.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Atmos for Business is the small business rewards program of Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines, and it runs parallel to the Atmos Rewards program (Atmos for Business used to be known as the EasyBiz program).
    • In a recent development, most major US airlines have a small business rewards program, and the intent is to offer extra rewards when businesses book travel.
    • Along those lines, in light of the recent refresh of the Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card (learn more), I think this program is worth a close look.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Atmos for Business is the small business rewards program of Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines, and it runs parallel to the Atmos Rewards program (Atmos for Business used to be known as the EasyBiz program).

    In a recent development, most major US airlines have a small business rewards program, and the intent is to offer extra rewards when businesses book travel. The good news is that even small businesses qualify for this, and it can really boost the rewards you earn.

    Along those lines, in light of the recent refresh of the Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card (learn more), I think this program is worth a close look. Long story short, Atmos Rewards members could be earning up to 23.5x points per dollar spent on airfare. Based on my valuation of 1.5 cents per Atmos Rewards point, that’s the equivalent of a jaw dropping 35.25% return on eligible spending. That’s simply unrivaled.

    Atmos for Business is the self-managed business travel program by Alaska and Hawaiian, intended for small and medium sized businesses.

    According to recent reports, the program is open to companies and organizations with at least $5,000 in annual travel spending, so if you’re a frequent flyer with the firm and have a small business, that’s not much of a hurdle. You can add an unlimited number of employees to your account, and all of their spending counts toward that requirement.

    Now, the terms suggest that you must have spent at least $5,000 or more on eligible Alaska and Hawaiian travel in the last 15 months, though in practice, that’s not directly enforced, best I can tell. After all, this is even intended to attract latest businesses that may be looking to switch travel to Alaska or Hawaiian.

    When a business enrolls in Atmos for Business, it’s assigned a company Atmos Rewards loyalty number. Atmos for Business then offers an impressive number of bonus rewards:.

    Beyond increased loyalty benefits for the business, Atmos for Business offers a platform that is supposed to make booking easier, with features like the following:.

    In a recent development, the total number of points that you can earn per dollar spent with Atmos for Business is pretty incredible, assuming you have the Atmos Rewards Business Card. As of 2027, Atmos Rewards members can choose how they get rewarded for flying, and they can choose to earn rewards based on distance flown, dollars spent, or segments flown.

    Assuming you choose to earn based on how much you spend, here’s how the math works out:.

    As you can see, a non-elite member booking through the Atmos for Business portal and paying with the Atmos Rewards Business Card would earn 15x points per dollar spent, while a Titanium member booking through the Atmos for Business portal and paying with the Atmos Rewards Business Card would earn 22.5x points.

    This doesn’t factor in the extra 1x points that the company earns, for a total of up to 23.5x points per dollar spent. Furthermore, it doesn’t factor in the 10% status points bonus, but that’s a different story.

    While I’m going for top tier Atmos Rewards Titanium status, I still don’t fly with Alaska or Hawaiian often, given that I live in Miami, so it’s not the most practical carrier. Still, my goodness, the return on airfare spending is absolutely unreal here, if you are a loyalist.

    This included the country my business is registered in, my business name, my tax ID, my phone number, and my address.

    It was that easy, and I was registered instantly. The Atmos for Business program account management page looked mighty familiar, as it’s basically the same concept as the American AAdvantage Business program. There you can add travelers, manage payments, etc.

    Sources indicate that to actually book travel, you just select the “Book Travel” heading. That will bring you to a search that looks identical to what you’ll find on Alaska’s website, but it’s customized to Atmos for Business.

    Pricing is identical to what you’d find directly on the websites of Alaska or Hawaiian, so that’s pretty tough to beat.

    Atmos for Business is the small business rewards program of Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines. Even small businesses qualify, though the idea is that it’s for those who spend at least $5,000 per year on flights with the firm across employees, which isn’t a very high bar.

    In a recent development, the main advantage of Atmos for Business is that you earn one extra point per dollar spent, plus 10% bonus status points. But the area where the program gets really rewarding is if you have the Atmos Rewards Business Card, as that offers 10x points per dollar spent through Atmos for Business.

    If you were an Atmos Rewards Titanium member booking through Atmos for Business and paying with the Atmos Rewards Business Card, you’d potentially earn a total of 23.5x points per dollar spent on airfare, with no caps. This is simply an amazing rate of return. Man, I’m really bummed that I can’t fly with Alaska or Hawaiian more, as that return on spending is something to get excited about.

    What do you make of the Atmos for Business program?

    • An American who was reportedly yelling at staff at a hotel in Thailand ended up picking a fight with the wrong guest, and it ended up costing him his life.
    • Media in Thailand is reporting on an incident that happened early this morning (Sunday, November 22, 2026), whereby a 46-year-old American tourist died at a hotel in Bangkok’s Phra Khanong area, after an altercation with a 39-year-old Italian man, who was reportedly an MMA fighter.
    • According to recent reports, according to the initial police report, the American had been arguing loudly with the hotel staff at the reception desk, for reasons that are unclear as of now.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    An American who was reportedly yelling at staff at a hotel in Thailand ended up picking a fight with the wrong guest, and it ended up costing him his life. This is both tragic and insanely irresponsible on both sides… I just don’t get what people are thinking sometimes….

    Media in Thailand is reporting on an incident that happened early this morning (Sunday, November 22, 2026), whereby a 46-year-old American tourist died at a hotel in Bangkok’s Phra Khanong area, after an altercation with a 39-year-old Italian man, who was reportedly an MMA fighter.

    According to recent reports, according to the initial police report, the American had been arguing loudly with the hotel staff at the reception desk, for reasons that are unclear as of now. As an Italian hotel guest walked past him and attempted to enter an elevator, the American reportedly grabbed him and pulled him out.

    In a recent development, the confrontation escalated, and turned into a physical struggle, during which the Italian man placed the American man in a chokehold, until he lost consciousness. Hotel staff called emergency services, and while first responders performed CPR, the American couldn’t be revived. Police also found an abrasion on the victim’s forehead.

    Recent findings suggest that the Italian man remained at the scene, and told authorities that he had been acting in self-defense, after being attacked. Police took him into custody, and he potentially faces manslaughter charges, though the case is still being investigated.

    The hotel at which this incident happened hasn’t yet been named, but this occurred at Sukhumvit Soi 48 — there are several hotels in that area, with the biggest “brand name” property being a Ramada Plaza by Wyndham.

    Industry observers note that I feel horribly for the family of the person who lost his life. I would have to imagine that odds are high that there were likely some substances involved here, and that this all happened after a substantial Saturday night out. After all, most people aren’t looking to get into a massive fight while getting their first cup of coffee in the morning (or maybe it’s just me?).

    But my gosh, the “victim” here sounds like he was acting absolutely horribly, arguing with hotel staff, and then picking a fight with a random person. At the same time, that also doesn’t justify the response of getting into a conflict that leads to a fatality.

    I absolutely love Thailand — the people are so friendly, the food is amazing, and the country also offers such diversity in terms of landscape, whether you want a city, a jungle, or a beach. However, there’s also no denying that the country (and particularly Bangkok) attracts a large percentage of tourists who are looking for debauchery.

    None of this has anything to do with a conflict that gets to the point of costing someone their life, but I can’t help but mention that when I review hotels, I tend to take a lot of pictures in lobbies around 4-5AM, when it’s the emptiest (since I’m a morning person anyway). Virtually everywhere else in the world, there’s not a single soul awake in public. Bangkok is probably the one exception, where you see a countless number of people moving through lobbies, elevators, etc., engaged in various forms of “business.”.

    An American man lost his life in Bangkok early on Sunday morning, after picking a fight with the wrong person. The 46-year-old was reportedly shouting at hotel staff, and then attacked a 39-year-old Italian guest getting into the elevator unprovoked. That Italian man was reportedly an MMA fighter, who put him in a chokehold, to the point that the American lost his life. While the man claims he was acting in self defense, he now potentially faces manslaughter charges.

    According to recent reports, it’s really sad how people act sometimes. We only have one life to live, and how unfortunate to cut your life short so unnecessarily.

    #134097. Southwest Aims To End The Wait For Extending Its Schedules—11 Month Rolling Calendar Is Coming, Report Says

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Viewfromthewing ↗ Open Full Page

    Southwest Aims To End The Wait For Extending Its Schedules—11 Month Rolling Calendar Is Coming, Report Says

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4197 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that southwest Airlines intends to stop making customers wait for batches of upcoming flight dates and move to a rolling booking calendar roughly 11 months into the future, more like other airlines operate, according to a new report by Enilria.
    • I checked Southwest’s own booking calendar.
    • In a recent development, there’s some history here that helps explain what’s changing.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that southwest Airlines intends to stop making customers wait for batches of upcoming flight dates and move to a rolling booking calendar roughly 11 months into the future, more like other airlines operate, according to a new report by Enilria. That would make it easier to lock in a family vacation or flights to a cruise—and give its international partners more opportunities to sell trips that include Southwest connections. I checked Southwest’s own booking calendar. They’re accepting reservations through September 29, 2027. Their next extension is planned for December 17, when they’ll open flights through November 6, 2027. That’s 324 days into the future. That December release is still a batch. The plan to replace these releases with a rolling window isn’t something I’ve seen anywhere other than from Enilria. Southwest Has Already Sold Flights More Than 300 Days Ahead There’s some history here that helps explain what’s changing. On April 26, 2024, Southwest unveiled its first booking window exceeding 300 days. It was selling travel through March 5, 2025—313 days ahead. At the time, Southwest mentioned its historical range had been 180 to 250 days, citing vacation planning, meetings and groups, Hawaii, and its international destinations as reasons to sell further out. With batch releases, though, the window shrinks every day until the next extension. You might be able to book ten months ahead on release day, then considerably less several weeks later. A rolling calendar keeps adding dates. The reported change would give customers roughly the same planning horizon whenever they shop, without needing to track Southwest’s next release announcement. Shorter Schedules Meant Fewer Reservations To Fix I wrote about Southwest’s tradeoff back in 2020: waiting to publish let the airline offer a firmer schedule, but cost them customers who wanted to commit earlier. An airline can decide where to put its planes before selling the seats, or sell a provisional schedule and fix customers’ reservations when its plans change. Southwest preferred to finish more of that work first. That gave them room to adjust for seasonal demand and aircraft availability without disrupting as many purchased trips. Their technology made changing flights expensive. In a 2010 investor presentation, then-CEO Gary Kelly explained that when Southwest canceled a flight: we have to manually rebook every single customer on that flight Southwest completed its move to Amadeus Altéa in May 2017. This allowed for automated rebooking during disruptions, better connection planning, and more sophisticated inventory management. So the technology that makes a longer selling window practical has been there for years. The commercial case for using it has grown. International Partners Have A Reason To Want More Dates Southwest increasingly needs to appear wherever customers are shopping. I explained how the Expedia deal would change their incentives when it was announced in 2025. If a customer searches dates Southwest isn’t selling, competitors get the business before Southwest even enters the comparison. The airline had already expanded booking capabilities through agency reservation systems in 2020. More recently, SAP Concur shut down its old Southwest direct connection in July 2025 as Southwest’s new fare structure required a different booking path. And Southwest now lists 12 international airline partners, including Icelandair, EVA Air, Singapore Airlines, Turkish Airlines, and newly added French bee. These combined itineraries are sold through the partners’ websites and distribution channels. A foreign airline can have its flight available for sale while Southwest hasn’t opened the domestic connection yet. The partner can’t issue the complete itinerary using that Southwest flight. It may sell a connection on another U.S. airline instead and Southwest loses the passenger. That makes partner sales a strong reason to extend the window. The underlying partnership work also predates Elliott Management’s intervention. I covered Southwest recruiting to build airline partnerships in June 2022. And the longer schedule announcement came in April 2024. Even a roughly 330 day window won’t match every overseas partner. EVA Air sells flights up to 360 days ahead. This would narrow the gap, while still leaving some early international bookings out of Southwest’s reach. Earlier Booking Comes With More Time For Plans To Change Selling earlier gives Southwest more chances to win customers. Direct bookings bring cash in sooner. The recurring benefit comes from business Southwest otherwise would’ve lost, or from selling its existing seats more profitably. Against that are distribution costs, servicing reservations, and the work of repairing itineraries when schedules change. Customers should expect more exposure to schedule revisions when booking further ahead. A departure can move, a nonstop can become a connection, and a changed domestic flight can break the connection to an international departure. With assigned seating, moving passengers also means dealing with their seat selections. And the first day a flight goes on sale isn’t necessarily its cheapest day. Opening dates and opening inexpensive inventory are separate decisions. In fact, airlines may hold back cheap fares waiting to see how flights sell, and also figuring that eager buyers may be less price-sensitive. And there’s a real a problem buying Southwest’s cheapest cash tickets this far ahead. As I’ve covered before, Basic fare credits expire six months after the original purchase. Southwest says a voluntary cancellation after that deadline produces no flight credit. If you buy a Basic ticket 11 months ahead, then cancel two months before departure, you’ve already passed that deadline by three months. The original reservation is valid, but you get nothing if you cancel. I’d be much more comfortable using Rapid Rewards points for a speculative booking that far out. Cancel at least 10 minutes before the original departure and the points go back to the account, without the six month expiration attached to the cash fare.     7 ways airlines are upgrading the flying experience in economy

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (162 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thepointsguy

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
  • Airlines are introducing notable innovations in economy cabins, including improved Wi-Fi, enhanced headrests and walk-up snack bars.
  • New seating concepts such as convertible couches and bunk beds are being rolled out to make long-haul flights more comfortable for economy passengers.
  • On-board wellness zones and upgraded entertainment systems, including Bluetooth connectivity and streaming partnerships, are becoming more common on select routes.
  • These changes aim to enhance the overall passenger experience without requiring travelers to pay premium cabin prices.
  • Some upgrades, like bunk beds or convertible couches, are available only on select aircraft and routes and may require an additional fee.
  • Access to free Wi-Fi often requires membership in an airline's loyalty program.
  • Entertainment and wellness features are being rolled out gradually, so availability may vary depending on the airline and specific flight.

    #134095. Tech Report: Masked ICE Agents Disrupt Alaska Airlines Boarding—Crew Too Shaken To Continue The Flight

    Tech Report: Masked ICE Agents Disrupt Alaska Airlines Boarding—Crew Too Shaken To Continue The Flight

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5380 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Passengers boarding Alaska Airlines flight 1306 from Seattle to Los Angeles on Saturday found themselves in a crowded jet bridge with masked federal agents struggling with travelers at the aircraft door.
    • An airport is almost the ideal place to arrest someone.
    • But those systems were built to protect aviation and travelers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Passengers boarding Alaska Airlines flight 1306 from Seattle to Los Angeles on Saturday found themselves in a crowded jet bridge with masked federal agents struggling with travelers at the aircraft door. Flight attendants were so shaken the airline needed replacements. An airport is almost the ideal place to arrest someone. The government has everyone’s travel information in advance, checks their identity, screens them for weapons, and knows where they’re going to be. There are cameras everywhere, and myriad law enforcement agencies on site. But those systems were built to protect aviation and travelers. Repurposing them for routine immigration ambushes creates a distraction from safety. What happened on that Alaska Airlines jet bridge The confrontation happened around 8 a.m. on November 21 at Seattle’s gate N9. The Port of Seattle says it involved Immigration and Customs Enforcement and two passengers, a father and daughter. There were roughly 50 people pressed against the jet bridge walls during a confrontation lasting more than 10 minutes. A pilot left and two flight attendants asked to be replaced. His original post is here. The flight, scheduled for 8:10 a.m., departed nearly three hours late. Watch the jet bridge video shared by KUOW reporter Kate Stone. Why the airport is such an attractive place for ICE An airport is a chokepoint, and the government has already done much of the work of locating and identifying a traveler. They know the itinerary. Airlines provide the Transportation Security Administration with passenger identifying information and flight details. There’s an identity check and weapons screening. Travelers funnel through controlled checkpoints and then present themselves at an assigned gate. That makes them easier to find and reduces some risks to arresting officers. There’s already substantial law enforcement. Seattle has its own Port police department, with about 120 commissioned officers across its airport and maritime responsibilities, alongside federal agencies operating at the airport. There’s DEA, FBI, TSA, CBP, local police and more. I’ve covered how passenger data collected for aviation security is being used to locate people for immigration arrests. There’s now a data sharing agreement between TSA and ICE. This is helpful to ICE, but adds no benefit to aviation security. A system justified by protecting passengers from terrorists and weapons is being repurposed to produce immigration arrests. That pulls crew and airport staff into confrontations, disrupts flights, and undermines trust in the security process. A crowded jet bridge is an especially bad place to create a struggle. Passengers have little room to move. Crew attention gets diverted from boarding and safety duties. Here flight attendants were too shaken to work afterward. There was no immediate threat to justify this intervention. A work permit matters, even when it doesn’t settle immigration status In the video, a woman says, “We have a work permit.” Work authorization and lawful immigration status are separate challenges. A person can have permission to work while an immigration case remains unresolved. While work permits have historically been issued pending adjudication of status, this administration acted on the status matter alone. But that doesn’t justify a jet bridge ambush. If someone has a valid work permit, the government has already dealt with them through a formal process and authorized their employment. Someone traveling openly under their own identity on a domestic ticket isn’t demonstrating an intent to disappear. Absent a specific danger or concrete reason to expect flight from the legal process, there’s a much stronger case for arranging an interview or pursuing the case through ordinary procedures than for a physical confrontation among boarding passengers. The government’s choice to treat they’ve even authorized to work as an emergency is patently ridiculous. This goes beyond a dispute over whether ICE can enter an airport Airport ambushes aren’t newly introduced: A U.S. citizen confronted while boarding a Delta Air Lines flight, apparently mistaken for a British man with the same name and birth date. A violent Las Vegas airport encounter that left a traveler with one handcuff attached after agents departed. He was subsequently arrested in Los Angeles. A state trooper arrested at the Madison airport despite holding work authorization, then released after a congressman intervened. What stands out in Seattle is the reported combination of a struggle in a packed jet bridge, passengers being deplaned, crew members needing replacements, and an airline and airport publicly questioning whether agreed procedures were even being followed. The Port of Seattle explains that federal agencies have broad airport access. It says its police don’t assist civil immigration enforcement. Alaska Airlines says: We are concerned by this morning’s law enforcement action during the boarding of Alaska Flight 1306. We recognize how distressing this incident has been for employees and guests. Alaska Airlines is required to comply with applicable laws and regulations when interacting with law enforcement officials. We do not direct or coordinate immigration enforcement activity, and we remain committed to protecting the privacy and safety of our guests and employees wherever possible. The airline also says it received no advance notice and is examining what happened and whether proper protocols were followed. Its statement continues: We will work with the Port of Seattle and government authorities to ensure the collaborative standards and practices that have kept our air system safe and secure for decades are respected moving forward. The Port of Seattle’s full statement: We are outraged about this morning’s incident involving ICE and two passengers as travelers boarded AS 1306 to Los Angeles. Immigration enforcement actions at SEA are conducted without the Port’s participation or knowledge. The Port has continually asked, and local federal immigration authorities have previously agreed to protocols at SEA, and we are in conversation with DHS on whether any of these protocols were breached. However, the Port remains committed to the safety of all of our travelers and staff and airline team. This incident was not only distressing for the affected family but the passengers around them, and Port officials continue to engage federal officials to understand more about what occurred. Association of Flight Attendants president Sara Nelson wrote, “Get the hell out of our airports, ICE! DHS, stop your terror campaign!” I liked her tweet. Sara Nelson’s response to the Seattle airport incident, November 21, 2026. Trump Is Using Software Words While ICE Escalates In his post-election interview aired November 8, President Trump acknowledged his deportation approach was excessive: “I think it might be too tough, yeah.” He also acknowledged it contributed to historic electoral rejection. Yet the White House unveiled Stephen Miller – the architect of the harshest treatment of foreigners – promotion to chief of staff on November 6.     💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that the catastrophic midterm results dealt to Republicans two weeks ago threaten but do not ultimately negate the conservative policy landscape as it stands two years into President Trump’s second term.
    • The border has been secured, deportations have been carried out at a high rate, federal agencies have been forced to abandon much of their institutional commitment to DEI and financial support of the left-wing NGO complex, universities have been put on notice that federal funding is not unconditional, and the administrative state has undergone its most serious shake-up in generations.
    • Inez Feltscher Stepman is a senior policy and legal analyst at the Independent Women's Forum.

    It has been revealed that the catastrophic midterm results dealt to Republicans two weeks ago threaten but do not ultimately negate the conservative policy landscape as it stands two years into President Trump’s second term. As I wrote before the election, many aspects of this administration are clearly good from the conservative perspective, not just by comparison to the Biden administration, but to Trump’s own first term and previous Republican administrations since the days of Ronald Reagan.

    The border has been secured, deportations have been carried out at a high rate, federal agencies have been forced to abandon much of their institutional commitment to DEI and financial support of the left-wing NGO complex, universities have been put on notice that federal funding is not unconditional, and the administrative state has undergone its most serious shake-up in generations.

    Inez Feltscher Stepman is a senior policy and legal analyst at the Independent Women's Forum.

    On “Can Trump’s Agenda Survive the Blue Tsunami?”.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, there’s something I really love about staying in a hotel room on a really high floor, where you’re so high up that you almost feel like you’re in an airplane.
    • Sources indicate that the question of which hotel is the tallest and highest isn’t as straightforward as you might assume.
    • Sources indicate that generally speaking, the tallest hotel would be defined as the tallest building where a large percent of the structure is made up of the hotel.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, there’s something I really love about staying in a hotel room on a really high floor, where you’re so high up that you almost feel like you’re in an airplane. So, what are the tallest and highest hotels in the world? I want to talk about that in this post, and also discuss why the answer isn’t that straightforward.

    Sources indicate that the question of which hotel is the tallest and highest isn’t as straightforward as you might assume. And even once we do define it, there’s the question of the extent to which the answer is actually useful. First let’s cover the distinction between the tallest hotel and the highest hotel.

    Sources indicate that generally speaking, the tallest hotel would be defined as the tallest building where a large percent of the structure is made up of the hotel. Most commonly, I see people suggest that this would include situations where at least 80% of the building is the hotel.

    This is different than the highest hotel, which would be the hotel that is highest above the ground, even if it only takes up a small percentage of a mixed-use building, where there might be apartments, residences, etc.

    In other words, a 50-story building that consists exclusively of a hotel would fall into the former category, while a 110-story building where the top 10 floors are a hotel would fall into the latter category.

    With that out of the way, let’s talk about the properties that are remarkable in these categories….

    Sources indicate that first, let’s cover some of the world’s tallest hotels. We’ll define this as hotels where at least 80% of the building consists of the hotel facility.

    Let me of course mention one downside of very tall standalone hotels — you could end up being on a very low floor. After all, if a high-rise consists exclusively (or almost exclusively) of hotel facilities, some people will end up on very low floors. The other downside, of course, is that these hotels are necessarily huge. If you prefer boutique hotels, you won’t find any on this list.

    Right now, the tallest hotel in the world is Ciel Tower Dubai. The 1,042-room hotel opened in 2024, rises to a height of 1,227 feet (374 meters), and has 82 floors.

    To go over the list of the top five tallest hotels in the world:.

    As you can see, it’s interesting (but perhaps not surprising) that all four of the world’s tallest hotels are in Dubai.

    Sources indicate that the Conrad Shanghai, meanwhile, is located in the Shimao International Plaza, and this is the perfect example of how it’s tough to define what is technically the tallest. While the building it’s in rises to such a high height, roughly 25% of that height is the spire. So technically it’s a very tall building, but the usable space isn’t as high as you’d assume.

    Industry observers note that if you ask me, the world’s highest hotels are much more interesting than the world’s tallest hotels. That’s because the world’s highest hotels typically take up the top floors of some gravity-defying skyscrapers, and therefore, they can also be boutique properties.

    When defining the world’s tallest hotels, there are some general challenges:.

    Because of the above, there are some minor disagreements as to which hotel wins the title, but I’ll share my take (while acknowledging that I don’t have the ability to scale buildings with a measuring tape).

    Recent findings suggest that presently, the highest hotel is the Rosewood Guangzhou. The 251-room hotel opened in 2019, and it’s located at the top of the CTF Finance Centre Guangzhou, which reaches a height of 1,739 feet (530 meters).

    To go over the list of the top five highest hotels in the world:.

    As you can see, those last two properties are kind of hard to judge, and particularly J Hotel Shanghai is tricky, given that the property is split between different parts of the building.

    Sources indicate that as the inverse of the above, I should mention that the Armani Hotel Dubai is located within the Burj Khalifa, which is the world’s tallest building. However, it’s located at the very bottom of the building, so that’s hardly that useful, for these purposes, since the hotel only goes as high as 39 floors.

    Lastly, in the interest of being thorough, if we’re going to define a hotel as being “highest” based on the altitude above sea level, then we’d of course end up with a completely different list. Hotel Tayka del Desierto is located near the Salar de Uyuni salt flats in Bolivia. It’s at an altitude of 14,800 feet (4,500 meters), so it’s generally considered to be the highest up hotel in the world.

    I suppose depending on how we want to define “hotel,” there would probably be some simple guest houses at Everest Base Camp that go even higher, but I don’t think that’s within the spirit of what I’m trying to cover here.

    It has been revealed that if you ask me, it’s always fun to stay in a hotel room that’s really high up. There’s an crucial distinction between the tallest hotels and the highest hotels, though sometimes, the exact rankings are a bit blurred.

    While I’ve long been interested in this, I enjoyed researching this a bit more closely, and actually having a (sort of) definitive list. Ciel Tower Dubai is the world’s tallest hotel, while the Rosewood Guangzhou is the world’s highest hotel (unless you want to consider the 120th floor of the J Hotel Shanghai separately from the rest of the property).

    Industry observers note that I used to request high floors specifically, but funnily over the years, it's something I don't really care about too much anymore. The main advantage of high floors in massive cities to me is that it's quieter, with less road noise. However, I generally dislike sky lobbies, especially if I have to take multiple elevators to get to my room. In some cities, it can be nice for the views, but often it's more of an inconvenience to me.     #134092. Latino Democrats celebrate midterm gains, with warning for party

    Latino Democrats celebrate midterm gains, with warning for party

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (692 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sánchez, here at a 2020 news conference in the Capitol Visitor Center, is the chair of BOLD PAC.
    • Latino voters moved sharply away from Republicans this year, and a record number of Latino Democratic candidates were elected.
    • Sánchez has a warning for her fellow Democrats.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    California Rep. Linda T. Sánchez, here at a 2020 news conference in the Capitol Visitor Center, is the chair of BOLD PAC. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    Latino voters moved sharply away from Republicans this year, and a record number of Latino Democratic candidates were elected.

    But California Rep. Linda T. Sánchez has a warning for her fellow Democrats.

    “Latino voters gave Democrats a two-year lease, but it expires in 2028 unless the party changes its playbook for good,” noted Sánchez, who leads the campaign arm of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus.

    Failure to address rising costs and push back against President Donald Trump’s immigration agenda could once again scramble the political calculus and spark another realignment in two years, noted House Democratic Caucus Chair Pete Aguilar of California.

    “While Latinos shifted towards Democrats and … gave us this mandate as a party, Democrats must continue to earn their trust, not just every two years, but every single day,’’ he stated.

    It has been revealed that leaders of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus joined newly elected Latino members on Tuesday for a news conference to celebrate the recent wins and the role the group played in securing the House majority for Democrats. The caucus will boast 55 members in the next Congress, its largest roster ever, according to Sánchez.

    BOLD PAC, the caucus’ campaign arm, invested heavily in Latino candidates this year, including in primaries.

    Sources indicate that california Rep. Salud Carbajal noted that BOLD PAC raised more than $18.5 million this cycle, which helped candidates leverage outside money.

    Working-class majority-Latino districts in South Texas, Arizona and California were among the areas that provided Democrats with their biggest wins. Democrats capitalized on voter dissatisfaction over rising costs, the very issue that helped Trump and the GOP make significant gains among Hispanic voters just two years earlier.

    But the wins weren’t limited to districts with sizable Latino populations.

    Rep.-elect Denise Powell, who flipped a swing seat in Nebraska, credited BOLD PAC for playing a key role in her win.

    Sources indicate that “Yes, there are Latinos in Omaha, and those Latinos actually helped decide this race,’’ she stated. “BOLD believed in me as a candidate, but they also believed in our community.”.

    Rep.-elect Bobby Pulido, who came to politics after a successful career as a Latin Grammy-winning Tejano singer, flipped a redrawn South Texas border district that Trump would have carried by 18 points in 2024.

    “A lot of people feel like they don't belong to either party. But there's one thing about Latinos is we belong to each other,’’ Pulido mentioned. “It's very hard to be a Latino right now in this country. … I expect to see us united, more united than ever, because it's a tough time right now.”.

    Several of the winning candidates deployed novel strategies to reach voters. Pulido famously began performing at quinceañeras after his Republican opponent dismissed him as a performer.

    Colorado Rep.-elect Manny Rutinel, who flipped a battleground district north of Denver, attended World Cup and Broncos watch parties. “If people don't hear our message, then it doesn't matter,’’ he remarked.

    Recent findings suggest that the candidates “met those voters where they were,’’ Sánchez remarked. “They went into those communities and interacted in a very real and meaningful way. That's something I think that strategists or consultants don't always get. It's not just about pumping out lots of television commercials.”.

    Amid those successes for Latino Democrats, Florida, home to one of the largest Latino electorates in the country, was a different story. Republicans held all three majority-Latino districts in the Sunshine State, though former news anchor Eliott Rodriguez, the son of Cuban immigrants, came within half a percentage point of unseating GOP Rep. María Elvira Salazar in a district that backed Trump by 15 points in 2024.

    Sources indicate that BOLD PAC did have a victory to celebrate in Florida, with Rep. Darren Soto, the deputy chair of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, narrowly prevailing in a district that Republicans redrew as one that no longer had a Latino majority.

    “The redistricting wars ended up failing because of the investment by BOLD PAC,’’ Soto remarked.

    • Sources indicate that A Frontier Airlines passenger indicates she refused to get off her San Francisco–Denver flight until a flight attendant apologized to her four year old son.
    • I don’t think asking for a little help with a frightened child is outrageous.
    • It has been revealed that she says her son was afraid of loud toilet flushes and needed the bathroom about 40 minutes before landing.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that A Frontier Airlines passenger indicates she refused to get off her San Francisco–Denver flight until a flight attendant apologized to her four year old son. The argument began with a request to flush the toilet after the frightened boy had left the lavatory. The mother says things escalated when she overheard the crew member making fun of his fear. I don’t think asking for a little help with a frightened child is outrageous. If the flight attendant mocked him, an apology was appropriate. But the mother wasn’t entitled to make getting off the aircraft conditional on receiving one. She says her son was afraid of loud toilet flushes and needed the bathroom about 40 minutes before landing. She tried offering headphones and offering to flush for him. Eventually she reassured him that they could ask a flight attendant to help. She says she asked the flight attendant near the lavatory to flush after they’d washed their hands and left. The response was, He can flush it. It’s not that loud. The flight attendant added that this was a fresh plane. The mother says she dropped the request, but while she and her son were inside the lavatory, she heard the crew member talking to a colleague: Can you believe that mom? Scared of a toilet? Come on. She says her son heard it too and asked whether they were talking about him. The mother flushed the toilet herself, with her son waiting outside and the door closed. At deplaning she confronted the flight attendant and demanded an apology to the boy. She says the crewmember responded “Have a good day,” so she announced: I’m not getting off this airplane until you apologize to my son for literally making fun of him for being afraid of something. A pilot emerged from the cockpit, the flight attendant apologized, and she left. She also says a couple of passengers applauded and another mother praised her. She’s since posted a clarification: she says she also asked the flight attendant to stand with her son while she flushed. She also says her analytics show viewers watched an average of 23% of the original video and that’s why so many people seem to have missed that she did, in fact, flush the toilet herself. She wanted help pressing a button once they were away, or standing beside the child briefly. A polite refusal would be reasonable. In terms of what the flight attendant’s actual duty is, the union contract‘s article 23.I assigns general tidying and replenishing lavatory supplies, but says, “Flight Attendants will not clean the aircraft.” Pushing the button isn’t cleaning, but they don’t have broad lavatory duties. The claim that it’s a new airplane doesn’t mean the toilet isn’t loud. Aircraft vacuum toilets can be startling. Brigham Young University researchers spent two years developing a quieter aircraft toilet, citing parents’ concerns about children being afraid to use them. A quieter cabin can even make the flush stand out more. I’ve written about flight attendants mocking passengers for using the bathroom during boarding. The mother makes herself much harder to sympathize with in her video, though. She calls the employee an “old bitch” and tells her to “know your f’ing role.” I sided with the expectation that parents clean up after their children when Anthony Bass complained about his pregnant wife being asked to pick up their child’s popcorn on United. Parents should take responsibility. And her refusal to leave is absurd. Complain to the airline, don’t inconvenience other passengers trying to get off the plane.
